title: Marmot Men's Trient Jacket
description: The Marmot Trient is a serious, all-mountain winter sport jacket, combining the waterproof, breathable performance of the company's proprietary MemBrain material with Thermal R synthetic insulation, made from recycled fiber. Weight has been kept to a minimum, and an Angel-Wing Movement design allows the range of motion that's so crucial when you're attacking the mountain slopes or backcountry trails.FeaturesMarmot MemBrain waterproof/breathable fabricMicro-stitched and 100% seam-taped, two-layer constructionAttached storm hood with laminated brimPack Pockets with water-resistant zippersChest pocket with water-resistant zipperInterior mesh storage pocketInterior zippered pocketMoisture-wicking DriClime-lined chin guardElastic draw cord hem for adjustability in serious weatherAngel-Wing Movement allows full range of motion without jacket riding up29-inch center back length for size mediumOne-pound, 6.9-ounce weightProprietary MemBrain Strata material is designed for extreme waterproof performance.Marmot MemBrain Strata MaterialMarmot's proprietary waterproof/breathable fabric is built around a lamination technology that rates at an unheard of 20,000mm in waterproof performance and 20,000gr in breathability. The lightweight, packable fabric uses neither lining or three-layer construction similar to many other lamination processes. Rather, MemBrain Strata products have a 2.5-layer construction using non-organic particles on the inside of the lamination to increase durability and provide a dry touch, avoiding the dreaded "clammy jacket interior." The back print pattern is designed to optimize durability and breathability, improving abrasion test scores by up to five times.Thermal R InsulationThermal R is Marmot's proprietary family of polyester insulations specifically engineered to meet various needs from sleeping bags, to garments, to gloves, offering excellent warmth-to-weight, resilient mid loft, and durability.Lifetime WarrantyMarmot products include a limited lifetime manufacturer's warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.About MarmotIn April 1971, University of California Santa Cruz students Eric Reynolds and Dave Huntley were in Alaska on the Juneau ice fields for a Glaciology school project. This was where the idea of Marmot, originally a collegiate climbing club, began. Reynolds and Huntley soon began making prototypes of down products such as vests and sleeping bags in their dorm room in Santa Cruz. By the spring of 1973, Reynolds and Huntley partnered with fellow climber Tom Boyce to open a modest rental and retail location, named Marmot Mountain Works, in a 100-year-old building in Grand Junction, Colorado.Their first large order was for 108, as the producer called them, "very puffy jackets" for the movie The Eiger Sanction, with Clint Eastwood, which helped make down outerwear fashionable. In 1976, Marmot was one of the first companies to recognize the value of a new technology being developed by W.L. Gore & Associates. Marmot was soon producing waterproof Gore-Tex sleeping bags, with Reynolds and Huntley testing early prototypes by sleeping in meat lockers and under fire sprinklers, and later introduced the waterproof/breathable fabric into nearly all Marmot products.From humble beginnings, Marmot and its product line have grown over the years, and today the company is headquartered in Rohnert Park, California, with offices all over the world and distribution in more than 60 countries.

What crashed was a weather balloon manned by a couple of those distant ancestors of yours known as "Monkeys". Small wonder the government of sector 666, better known as The United States, wanted to keep it a secret. So would we, had we made such an elementary mistake to let a space flight be controlled by *our* ancestors (who were green jellyfish).The whole idea of us visiting your godforsaken planet is ridiculous in itself. By Jove and Sirius, who do you think you are, some kind of cosmic hot shots? Our flying saucers can travel a distance of 10,000 parsecs in the blink of an eye - why on earth do you think we would be interested in visiting your little cosmic backwater, when we can go boldly to much cooler places were no man will hopefully ever go? There *are* planets in the infinite universe that aren't plagued by roaches, mosquitoes, budget deficits and new episodes of "Haunted Highway", you know.We never met George Adamski or Billy Schmucking Meier, I mean, do you really think self-respecting Ascended Masters from the Pleiades would travel in ships that look like a birthday cake?! Or use ridiculous names such as Ptahotep, Ankh-A-Ra or Giza Sector 57? Besides, our names cannot be pronounced by earthlings, not even telepathically. reviewText: This poncho is a mix of good and bad things. Personally, the pros outweigh the cons and is a product that has a shot to prove itself.ProsLightweight- says the shipping weight is three pounds, I would say that it is lighter. Maybe one or two. Those that are concerned about the weight they carry can be rest assuredRip-stop- you can always be rest assured that if you...rip your poncho it won't continue to rip. Unfortunately, a poncho that is torn greatly diminishes the effectiveness of the poncho. The benefits of rip-stop is that it does make it tear resistantProvided Stuff Bag- I am on the fence about it. It is really gimmicky and mediocre in construction. The drawstring closures hardly work and rip the stitching if you pull too hard. What I like about it is that the poncho is stuffed into something that could easily fit the side pocket of cargo shorts/pants or a bag. It is roughly 8x7x2 (when stuffed) that could easily be compressed to a third of that with little effort.Additional Uses- Poncho "only" was the last thing on the designers mind. They were planning on it being used for a little bit of everything. A tent, floor mat, etc. This has button snaps to connect to other ponchos to provide a myriad of options. The grommeted corners are easily used for stakes and other things.Noise- It is noticeably more quiet than the normal plastic ponchos, which is nice from a tranquility aspect or any "ninja" activities you might want to do.Flecktarn- Flecktarn is one of the more difficult popular camo's out there, so options are very limited for my favorite military camo. Thank you Fox for making this.ConsSomewhat Expensive- At $30 this is one of the most expensive ponchos I have come across. Admittedly, I don't go chasing after ponchos all that often so it would be easy to say there are probably many more expensive ones out there. I have seen ponchos upwards of $50 but a majority are your $2 throwaways and commonly $10 and even $20.Length- It would have greatly benefited if it was 3-6 inches longer. Now I am taller than the Average Joe, but not unreasonably so. Expect it to be at knee height give or take 2-3 inches.Made in China- It makes me question the actual construction and quality of the product, as with all Chinese products.Lightweight- even this is a huge pro, this is a con. From experience, lightweight are weaker than your heavyweight counterparts. I am not sure about the true durability of the product. It says the product is waterproof, there is always the chance that the p/u coating skipped over the product, applied incorrectly, or would wear off eventually.

title: Casio Protrek PRW2500B-3 Altimeter Watch
description: Receive a constant flow of information about your location and environment without advertising your presence when you wear the Casio Protrek PRW2500B-3 Altimeter Watch on your wrist. This burly but smart mini-computer delivers the same information as its siblings in the Casio PRG2500 line, including a barometer, thermometer, altimeter, andcompass powered by Tough Solar Power; the difference is a camo package that is almost completely non-reflective so you don't attract attention as you check the watch for vital information.
reviewText: I am pleased with this purchase. The watch performs as advertised after setup. The camo band is understated, which I like. That is to say that it is unquestionably camo, but it does not attract attention as such like, say having every possible camo truck accesory or having a camo recliner in your living room might, if you know what I mean. The watch is a bit larger than I usually prefer, but it is not too large so as to be uncomfortable or attract too much attention. I have a medium/small wrist and fortunately the band fits without extending past the point where the elastic retainer can hold it. So far the rotating bezel has stayed put all but once, when it moved about 15 degrees - likely from going in and out of a pocket multiple times.The key here for me was to have a durable multi-function watch with the compass/alt/barometer functions that is cool looking but doesn't exist purely as a techie or outdoorsman status symbol. This watch was a bit more expensive than some other options, but I wanted a solar powered one that was perhaps a bit less obvious on the wrist than some other options. title: Lowepro LP36407-PAM Pro Messenger 180 AW Backpack (Slate Grey)
description: When your gear feels right, your work goes more smoothly. The Pro Messenger AW - a soft-sided bag that fits pro-sized gear - was designed with this idea in mind.
reviewText: The Lowepro Pro Messenger 180 AW is Lowepro's medium-sized bag from their Pro Messenger AW Series designed for professional DSLRs. It is taller than the 160AW but, otherwise, pretty much the same. Similarly, it is more bulky than many bags designed to carry a similar amount of gear.The exterior of the bag is made of a handsome sturdy polyester material that resembles canvas. It has a removable handle and a shoulder strap with a very comfortable, well-padded non-slip shoulder pad. The bag also has a zippered exterior sleeve on the back so you can attach it to the handle of rolling suitcases or zip it closed for additional storage. A very nice feature allows you to seal the bag's flap using either Velcro fasteners or, when silence is required, a section of the flap can be folded up so a magnetic clasp can be used instead. The flap covers the front pouch which holds a rain-cover and a zippered pouch with a number of interior pockets.The interior of the bag is very well-padded, sports a couple of handy pockets and includes 2 Velcro repositionable dividers. The resulting compartments are on the large side. There are also two small Velcroed compartment sub-dividers meant to be used horizontally, presumably for stacking gear.I transferred my 7D and a couple of lenses without attached hoods to the 180AW but found the lens compartments just a bit too big for my taste as many lenses tended to jostle or roll around a bit. This might not be much of an issue for you if you leave the lens hoods attached/reversed. As a positive, the 180AW, however, does fit the 7D with a 70-200 f/4L IS lens attached like a glove. Nice.All in all, its a very comfortable and extremely sturdy almost perfect bag with lots of handy features but it would hit perfection if you could just subdivide the compartments vertically for a better fit with some gear.

title: Shooting Chrony F-1 Chronograph (green)
description: The Shooting Chrony F1 Chronograph measures the speed of bullets and other projectiles. The Chrony F1 Chronograph Includes a jack for use with an optional Chrony Ballistic Printer (sold separately).
reviewText: I was very pleased with the results I got from this chronograph. I took it out into the woods and set it up. It was a moderately sunny day, and there were tree limbs overhead, but using the provided sunshades it gave me consistent results for loads out of my Marlin 1894 in .357 Magnum from about 15 feet away. They were also pretty much in-line with what my reloading manual said they should be, so I am pretty confident in the accuracy of the readings as well.I then switched to the same loads out of my 2-inch snubby revolver, and got errors from the first two shots...not too surprising to me considering the muzzle blast out of the snubby is pretty ridiculous. I backed up a few feet and it began registering the shots successfully. Then I let one of my rounds stray a bit to the left and hit one of the rods for the sunshade support. The sunshade went flying, but was unbroken. The rod was bent into a "u", but I straightened it out in my vise when I got home, and it's (almost) as good as new. I know there have been some complaints on here about the flimsiness of the sunshade, but you will be happy for that if you hit it...it keeps stuff from getting broken.Overall, I'm very pleased with this product. I did a significant amount of research before purchasing, because I'd read a lot of frustrated comments regarding chronographs in general. I didn't want to go cheap and get junk, but I didn't want to spend a bunch of money for something that didn't work any better than the cheaper option, either. I was very pleased with the results that I got from the chrony, especially considering that is is pretty much the cheapest option out there. When I did my part and put the rounds where they were supposed to go, it delivered accurate, consistent results. Great product...just don't expect it to be bulletproof :-).

title: Lowepro LP36408-PAM  Pro Messenger 200 AW Camera Bag (Slate Grey)
description: When your gear feels right, your work goes more smoothly. The Pro Messenger AW - a soft-sided bag that fits pro-sized gear - was designed with this idea in mind.
reviewText: I played around with this case for a while before figuring out the best use for it. I suspect it would be an ideal photojournalist's bag. There's room for a large pro DSLR, like a D2 or D3 or one of the pro-series Canons, complete with a big lens, a second lens, charger, spare SD cards, flash, batteries, a notebook or tablet and more. The inside is flexible and can be rearranged to suit your own needs; I found I could fit two complete M34 cameras and lenses, flash, spare batteries, charger, and a lot more.The exterior fabric is very tough, and obviously chosen for its abrasion resistance. This will survive years of heavy use. There's a hidden pull-oven rain cover, a feature pretty much common to all Lowepro bags these days, and an extremely clever bag flap that can be quickly arranged to use with either a very secure velcro closure or a quick magnetic closure.This is very much a walking-around bag and not a gear storage bag, although it can quickly be set up to ride on the extendable handle on a suitcase. It's a bag for the photojournalist who needs a system that keeps gear at hand while making sure it won'y fall out while running from a riot or chasing a politician.  Set it on the table, as another reviewer has noted, and it will tip over. But hanging from your shoulder it's one of the the best quick-access bags I've seen so far. Functionally, it reminds me of the canvas Domke bagsthat were almost ubiquitous in the camera corps in the 1980s.So: Great bag for the photographer on the go who needs a rugged bag that provides fast access, but won't let their gear fall out when they're sprinting across the tarmac. It would also work well as a large travel and camera bag or carryon bag, and that's what I plan on using it for.

reviewText: These socks are designed for people who sit or stand idly for periods of time and need some support to get the blood back up to the heart and brain. The low pressure and knee length ones are for relatively healthy and fairly active people. In the professional world these are known as anti-embolism socks. The object is to reduce the chance of an embolism (clot) from forming in the legs and traveling up to some more critical part of the body such as the lungs or even heart or brain. To the relatively healthy they do the same, but they also reduce the edema (fluid build up) in the legs which can even happen while walking on flat roads or trails. You might notice this as a slight aching in the legs as they will feel full or the skin feel stretched out and "tired". By having fluid in the legs it is not being recirculated back to the heart, etc, which robs the upper body of needed fluid. It also makes the legs heavier. In severe cases there can be up to 10 or 20 lbs in each leg of excess fluid (a very compromised patient). I remember many years ago hiking in the Grand Canyon from Hermits Rest along the Tonto trail, my legs began to feel tired and achy. I lay on the trail with my legs leaning up on the trunk of a Scrub Oak for a short break of about 20 minutes. The legs felt wonderful afterwards and I was able to then hike from below South Rim Village to Grand-view. Now I don't hike like that anymore just from a practical standpoint, but after a 13-14 mile hike recently, with the socks on, my legs were feeling much better than they would have, even to the point of jogging the last about 1.5 miles. I did not use them at a recent birthday party for a friend. At the end of the party my legs felt achy, stiff and full with a tight feeling.  That taught me a lesson to wear them at every opportunity. Don't wear them with your legs up for long periods as they can cut off the circulation.One thing negative I have noticed is that the socks slip somewhat inside my hiking shoes unless I use wool socks over the compression socks. Using both socks reduces the slipping, though the shoes need to be loosened some to accommodate the increased size. The wool helps to wick away sweat.
summary: Outstanding socks, but they slip some in the shoe.

reviewText: Here's the most important attribute that you need to know about this suitcase: It only weighs 8.5 pounds. This suitcase is primarily going to be a suitcase that you check on an airplane and you will need it to hold as much as possible up to the 50 pound airplane checked baggage limit. The less the suitcase weighs, the more that you can carry. This suitcase is about 8 pounds lighter than comparable suitcases, which means that you can carry 8 more pounds of your stuff (41.5 pounds of cargo vs. 35 pounds in a similar suitcase is an almost 20% increase in capacity). This is huge when you are trying to minimize the number of bags you have to pay to check!The overall size of this suitcase is not overwhelming, and it rolls well using the collapsable handle. It is very spacious on the inside. I think that this suitcase looks very attractive, but it is certainly not high end luggage. I value this luggage as a tool for carrying the most amount of cargo that I can on an airplane flight, and not as a status symbol. I also have the 22" matching version of this suitcase, and value it as a carry on bag also because it is so light.

title: Domke F-2 Original Bag (Black)
description: The bag that started it all. Jim Domke had the first one custom made for his own use in 1976, and theF-2is still one of the most popular Domke Bags today. Designed so that the photographer could get at equipment instantly, without having to take the bag from their shoulder. Includes an adjustable non-slip Gripper Strap with durable cotton webbing, removable bottom stiffener, removable hand carrying strap, YKK zippers, and steel snap hooks.
reviewText: I used Domke bags several years ago when I worked as a news photographer.  The design was/is one of the best around for a bag to work out of rather than just to carry equipment.  I liked the bag for its "floppiness" and its ability to mold itself to your body when carried.  The biggest problem with the bags--and I saw this in virtually every Domke bag being carried by news photographers at the time--was that they wore through due to friction.  Carrying it every day meant it rubbed against your side and mine eventually wore a big hole in the back.  The only other problem I had with the bag was the lack of weather proofing.  Being cotton, when they got wet they stayed wet for a long time.I switched to a waterproofed nylon bag but it had its own problems.  Zippers wore out and the rough nylon rubbed against and wore spots on my jackets.Bottom line is--there is no perfect camera bag.  The best I've found has been the Billingham brand (those are 5-star bags).  They are dense-weave cotton with a waterproofing applied.  They don't wear as easily and they don't absorb water.  They're as easy to work out of as a Domke.  They cost a LOT more, however.I like the Domke bags as a less expensive alternative to the Billinghams.  I still like to transport equipment in heavily padded, waterproof nylon bags but, more often than not, I'll carry a Domke or Billingham canvas bag when I'm actually shooting photos.
summary: It's not perfect but it's a good choice

reviewText: I want to make it clear that this review reflects my experience traveling through India, which is not exactly normal, everyday use.  If you read through some of the more glowing reviews, you will surely note that this is an -awesome- bag.  Wheeling it from the airport to home, this bag reigns supreme.  However, some rougher international travel brought about this bag's demise.First of all, when I picked my bag up from Delhi International, the top zipper had broken off.  I had placed a tiny travel lock to hold the two zippers together and when the bag showed up, both zipper pulls and the lock were gone.  Perhaps what I did constitutes abuse, which may be the case, but it would have been nice to have some proper zipper locking loops secure the bag.Next, after dragging the bag over rough ground and through a few ditches (pronounced, "Haridwar") the wheels began to bend outward.  Their days are numbered.  After noticing the wheels were on their way out, I started to use the backpack straps.  After a week or so, the buckle on the right side exploded while putting it on.  Towards the end of the trip, I was afraid to put anything in the bag and couldn't use the straps, so I ended up over-loading my smaller backpack to give the wheels a break.  This really defeats the purpose of having wheels in the first place!One last issue I have had is that the zipper, when the bag stands up, rubs on the ground.  The zipper on the bottom is beginning to ware.  As this zipper seems to be one continuous coil of plastic, when this goes out, the bag is effectively useless.  This ware is compounded when the bag's expansion zipper is out. I'm not sure how much life this bag has left in it!Over all, I expected a lot more out of this bag.  Taking it from baggage claim to the curb, it's a champion, but when asked to do a little work, it disintegrates.
summary: A month in India destroyed this bag

Brush the nap with the grain for a flat, softer look, or against the grain to create a brighter look. Pedag Nubuck Brush: Nubuck is one of the most expensive and beautiful types of leather. When you sand the outer layer of a hide until it is velvety soft with a visible nap you get nubuck. Pedag’s Nubuck Brush is the right tool for caring for nubuck. The brush is made of high quality crepe with enough grip to restore the nap to its original beauty. Use the nylon bristles to remove surface dirt and get into tight places on your shoe, garment or furniture and remove lodged in dirt. Crepe also produces a dry cleaning, eraser effect, which helps remove marks and stains without removing color. Use the nylon side again to restore the nap. Brush the nap with the grain for a flat, softer look, or against the grain to create a brighter look. Both brushes are made in Germany.

description: Swiss excellence built to go DEEP! Wenger AquaGraph 1,000m Diver's Watch for land and sea. reviewText: I have had this watch for two weeks now and am happy with it so far.  The buying experience with Amazon was smooth as usual.  The rubber band that came with it was too small (had to go to last two holes) so I put a 22mm steel bracelet from my old watch on it.  Much nicer with the stainless band.  If you want to go that route, then purchase the watch with the rubber strap and buy an aftermarket stainless steel bracelet (you can find them for around $50.00  then you have two bands and don't pay the extra 100 Wenger charges for the stainless bracelet.  The second hand doesn't line up exactly with the numerals on the dial, but it's a hair off and if you aren't anal about it, you probably won't notice.  It has kept time well (only lost 2 seconds in two weeks).  The warranty requires you have Wenger service it for the three year warranty period.  That means you must send it off to Wenger for battery replacement if it runs down before the time is up. My only other complaint is that it has a mineral crystal instead of a sapphire one, but only time will tell how resistant it is to scratching.  So, with a $450 retail value bought through Amazon for $230....I'm very happy with this watch and would recommend it to anyone.

title: Timex Women's T59201 Ironman 50-Lap Triathlon Sleek Resin Strap Watch
description: About Timex Timex Corporation is the nation's leading watch manufacturer. With a large and varied line of watches, Timex has the style for everyone. From the locker room to the board room, there's a great Timex time-piece for you. Look for Timex on the wrists of many great athletes competing in Ironman events world-wide. And like the best athletes, Timex keeps on ticking. Durable, lightweight resin case with strap. 50-lap memory recall. 100-hour chronograph with lap/split. Water-resistant up to 330 ft.. Dimensions: 9L x 1.25W x 0.5H in..
reviewText: I really like the functionality of the Ironman watches. I like this one in particular because it's on the smaller side. The watch features 3 alarms (with day-of-the-week options), 2 different count-down alarms (and one allows you to set multiple successive count downs of varying lengths), a stopwatch and 2 timezones. It's very easy to use, and gives instructions on how to set various things. I liked this watch so much that I bought a second after the first one broke.Unfortunately, every one of the Ironman watches I've owned have failed in the exact same way - the band. There are little rubber tabs that fit into the watch case, and they are the only thing that connects the band to the watch. If the rubber tabs get stretched or torn, then the watch case falls out. To be fair, the band is definitely comfortable, and the curvature of the band makes it fit sturdily without being too tight.The bands have lasted between 3-14 months, so I've been buying a new $30-$40 watch once a year (or so) for the past 6 years. I've been unable to find watch band replacements, and I'm not sure that I could do it myself anyway. The warranty specifically says that it does not cover any problems with the band of the watch. At this point, there's a clear financial incentive for Timex to pair awesome watches with bad bands. If you search the reviews for Ironman watches, so many people just buy a new watch when the watchband breaks, rather than try to get the band replaced. I'm boycotting the Ironman watches because of this.It looks like the Timex Expedition has most of the features I want, so that's what I'm going to get next.

title: Targus Terra Backpack Designed for 16-Inch Laptops - TSB226US (Black/Red Accents)
description: Terra Backpack with Rain CoverTerra Backpack with Rain CoverTSB226US
reviewText: UPDATE!It's well over a year since my initial review and since then I have gone back to school and I am now using this daily as my school/work backpack. I routinely carry two large textbooks, three notebooks, and a 14" laptop in this backpack, along with all my other belongings from my purse so I don't have to carry that around separately. It has ample room for everything I store in it and it's ergonomic design lessens the stress on my back and shoulders as well. From time to time, I do carry my 17" laptop in this backpack as well and it is close, but it does fit and I love that this backpack has so many uses for me. I'm going camping in October and I plan to bring all my necessities along in this backpack as well. Given it's size, it's able to hold a surprising amount of stuff and I've been known to wear it while crawling through tunnels and going down slides with my son when I have a hard time staying focused on my homework while he's having so much fun on the playground without me! Overall it's become such an integral part of keeping my daily life simple and organized and it's still going strong. No signs of wear anywhere and I expect it to last me the next four years of college as well. Thanks, Targus!-------------------------------------------------------One of the first things I noticed about this backpack is the generous padding on the back and shoulder areas. That has always been my number one gripe with backpacks of any kind. Over time they dig into your shoulders and if you have anything heavy in them (ie, a laptop!) the edge of it will rub against my back through the thin material of the backpack. The padding serves two purposes really, comfort and protection of your laptop. While I use my iPad primarily now for mobile computing, I do occasionally find the need to bring my laptop along. Even with only my iPad and accessories and no laptop, I find a lot of value in this backpack. It has an ample amount of organization, including a separate area for your laptop/iPad with a band that goes over the top of the device to ensure that even if the backpack is flipped upside down, your devices won't fall out. It's protected between the heavily padded back and a sturdy separator that keeps it from moving around or bumping into other things inside the backpack. The other side of this separator has plenty of room for books, accessories, or whatever else you might need to bring along with you. The front pouch also has lots of room for more storage and includes built in organizers for pens, notebooks and the like. On the very front is a small pouch that I like to put my bluetooth headset, speakers and chargers in. I love the side pockets too, that provide easy access to it's contents. Perfect place to slip a phone or your keys. Another great addition is the padded handle right between the shoulder straps for when you just want to carry it. Much nicer than toting it around by the shoulder strap. A little surprise bonus that I wasn't aware of was the zippered pouch on the very bottom of the backpack which stores an elasticized rain poncho for putting over the backpack if you get caught in some unfavorable weather. Nice touch! You can also easily slip a water bottle in here with the pouch present. More storage!On quality, just feeling it you can tell this is high quality, durable material. This isn't your $10 backpack from your local store! The stitching is high quality, no loose threads, no gaps in the stitches. I can't tell you how many backpacks we've had in this family over the years that start splitting seams, zippers falling off, etc, in just a year or two of regular use. I can tell the Terra Backpack is going to last much much longer.I mentioned the backpack is great for camping as well, and given it's cost I really think it should have multiple uses. I really can't see myself carrying this around on a regular basis due to its size (not any bigger than a traditional backpack, just bigger than what I need on a daily basis) but I can absolutely see myself using this on our annual camping trips. Plenty of room for all my supplies and durable to boot. The rain poncho would really come in handy here! The various clips and loops on the exterior of the backpack would also be very useful for attaching tools and utilities. Overall, I think it's worth the price if you are or have a full time student that regularly carries a laptop or if you do a lot of camping. I paid $20 for a backpack of similar size that is pretty much just flimsy fabric sewn in the shape of a backpack. The Terra Backpack is much more than this. Highly recommended!

description: Any child can be instantly transformed into an authentic Clone Trooper with the Hasbro Clone Wars Voice Changer Helmet. Designed for aspiring troopers aged five and up, this helmet is fun for adults, too..caption { font-family: Verdana, Helvetica neue, Arial, serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic; } ul.indent { list-style: inside disc; text-indent: -15px; } table.callout { font-family: verdana; font-size: 11px; line-height: 1.3em; } td.think { height: 125px; background: #9DC4D8 url(http://images.amazon.com/images/G/01/electronics/detail-page/callout-bg.png) repeat-x; border-left: 1px solid #999999; border-right: 1px solid #999999; border-bottom: 1px dotted #000000; padding-left: 20px; padding-right: 20px; padding-bottom: 10px; width: 250px; } td.glance { height: 100%; background: #9DC4D8; border-left: 1px solid #999999; border-right: 1px solid #999999; padding-top: 10px; padding-left: 20px; padding-right: 20px; padding-bottom: 10px; width: 250px; } img.withlink {border:1px black solid;}What We ThinkFun Factor:Durability:(what this means)The Good:Durable, realistic Clone Trooper helmetThe Bad:Size may be awkward for younger childrenIn a Nutshell:Inspires active, imaginative play that spans distant galaxiesAt a GlanceAges:5 and olderRequires:3 AA batteries (included)The mask is sure to please a Star Wars fan.View larger.The microphone inside changes and amplifies your child's voice.View Larger.Join the Grand Army of the RepublicPreparing for your first mission as a Clone Trooper is quick and easy. Before you assemble the helmet, adjust the straps on the insert to fit your child, then snap it into place. We had to try several times before the two back pieces and the front of the helmet snapped together neatly. Once we got the three pieces aligned correctly, they attached securely, producing a sleek, sturdy helmet. The three "AA" batteries that power audio features come already installed.Featuring realistic details, including a tinted visor, a crest on top, and clone-inspired colors, this durable, plastic helmet has three buttons on the right side that prompt five different sayings from the Clone Wars TV show. A button that issues radio static keeps communication interesting, and commands like "Cover Me!" and "All units fire at will!" add a quick adrenaline rush to any battle. Plus, there's a voice-modulator microphone so kids (and adults) can issue their own statements in a cool clone voice.Experience Intergalactic Role PlayingWhether part of a Halloween custom, an everyday role-playing game, or a display in the ultimate collector's bedroom, this Clone Trooper helmet brings home all the excitement of Star Wars. We were floored by the accuracy and durability of its construction. Plus the tinted visor was much easier to see through than we expected, as long as the helmet was sized correctly.The size and weight that make this helmet so realistic and durable did cause us to worry about how easy it would be for smaller children to wear. It's true that the straps inside adjust to fit small heads, but that doesn't prevent the size of the helmet itself from being awkward. Similarly, the microphone is adjustable, but it can still be stuck too far away from a small child's mouth. This means that the helmet has to be lifted by hand to speak through the microphone.When it's positioned close enough to the wearer's face, the microphone does a good job amplifying statements and commands, as well as providing the static you'd expect from a clone. It's ability to truly modify and deepen a voice is less reliable, although this doesn't really detract from the fun. Overall, it's hard to beat a toy that encourages active, imaginative play the way this helmet does. Even adults who are loyal to the original trilogy are likely to enjoy slipping the Clone Trooper helmet on and taking part in the struggles of the Republic.What's in the BoxClone Trooper helmet and instruction booklet.
reviewText: We decided to get this helmet for our 4 year old's halloween costume, rather then spend $15 for some cheapy costume mask.  Yes, it required patience to get out of the box, but most toys do.  Yes, it required even more patience to snap the pieces together, but following the directions help, and I found that when putting together the top and bottom of the back piece, if I slid the outside notches in on each side first, rather than doing the middle first, it worked out much better and made things alot easier.  Then it was easy enough to apply pressure to the middle to snap it together.  Putting together the front and back was pretty straightforward and did not require as much muscle.  My youngest son loves this helmet alot, and yes he does look like a bobble head, but with proper fitting of the multi-adjustable strap, it fits him comfortably and stays on his head with normal movement.  We ended up buying a second one for our 7 year old, and the experience I had with the first, cut down the assembly time to under 5 minutes.  Since I had read of problems a few others had with these staying together, I took care to assemble both correctly, and as a result we have had no issues with them coming apart and find them to be very sturdy.  The voice amplification microphone has to be pretty close to your mouth to really work properly, but the kids don't seem to care as much about that feature as they do the preprogrammed sayings.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

description: The Aegis Eyeshield offers maximized coverage and protection for high impact environments. reviewText: I have tried several glasses on the Army APEL list, and about the only ones worth recommending are the Oakley M Frames 2.0 and the ESS Crossbow for fit, comfort, and aesthetics.The Smith Aegis Arc has an extremely wide lens, that at first appearance, looks very protective. However, it allows for a rather large gap underneath where debris can and will strike at the eye. The nose pad is not comfortable and the Asian fit doesn't seem to be as good as Oakley's Asian fit (Oakley doesn't offer an Asian Fit M Frame, but the regular M Frame fits Asian heads/faces just fine).I do like how the Smith Ignitor lens is a mirror coated red lens. ESS's Copper and Oakley's VR28 are great, but I wish the Iridium/mirror coated versions were offered straight out for the APEL frames.That said, the Aegis is heavy at 45 grams. Oakley's Flak Jackets are 25 grams, the original M Frames with a Hybrid S lens are 25 grams. The Oakley M Frames 2.0 are 31 grams, and the ESS Crossbows are 35 grams. I honestly feel the Crossbows are at the limit for weight, and the M Frames 2.0 seem heavy as well inducing some fatigue after wearing them for 5-6 hours. There's a reason for the Aegis weighing 45 grams. The locking mechanism is made of thick plastic and has 2 metal screw/pivot points. In addition, the lenses are about twice as thick as the Oakley M Frames 2.0 lenses. I believe the MIL-STD for ballistic protection is why the lenses are so thick... I noticed the ESS Crossbow lenses to be thicker as well, while the regular Oakley Flak Jacket lenses seem paper thin by comparison.Overall: 1/5 stars. Too heavy, poor fit and coverage, and ugly design. I recommend looking at the ESS Crossbow or Oakley M Frames 2.0/3.0 instead

description: Detachable and adjustable shoulder strap, main compartment with zip closure, three external zip pockets, one exterior hook and loop pocket and key clip.
reviewText: I ordered this bag because I was tired of buying purses that were cute but basically useless and then switching to a bag that was handy and useful but generally ugly or looked like a diaper bag. While hiking one day I realized what I needed was a cross-body bag that could go from shopping to hiking easily. It needed to offer quick access to my cell-phone, camera, and GPSr unit, but it also needed to hold a notebook and pens, a bottle of water, and the typical mom-stuff that moms have to carry around. I tried a couple of hiking-specific bags, but they all were too rough and tumble. After poking around Amazon for hours one night, I came across the Cadilicious, and decided to give it a try. It came in a cute pattern (the one I have doesn't seem to be available as of the writing of this review, but the new ones here are quite cute!) and the reviews raved about it, so I ordered it. It arrived, and my first thought was "Oh, it's bigger than I thought. This won't work." But I loaded it up with all the necessary items, and gave it a try...it's amazing. I took it to a weekend getaway, and it went from the casino to the mountains to a resort to a sporting event with me, and it was amazingly useful every step of the way. I LOVE the size of the pockets, and how much stuff I can fit in it. It is a comfortable cross-body when I'm out all day, and the strap easily shortens to make it an over-the-shoulder bag when I'm running errands and hopping in and out the car all day. The back velcro pocket is perfect for keeping my lists and my sunglasses ready for a quick reach. The large main pocket tucks my emergency toiletries/necessities, face wipes for the kids, checkbook, and small notebook with room to spare. (This pocket came in very handy at a recent sporting expo--all the goodies and swag fit nicely in my bag and I didn't look like the freebies looter that I am!) The tall front pocket is perfect for easy retrieval of my wallet. The two smaller pockets on the front house my chapstick and lotion, my ID badge, and small snacks for the kids. I am very much looking forward to taking this bag to Disney in a few months!

description:

reviewText: The Global Vision LTD are, in my experience, the best motorcycle sunglasses for riders with contact lenses, hands down. Unless you ride with a full face helmet or face shield type helmet.  These eliminate the need for a face shield. I have tried countless other alternatives, short of the WileyX, and can honestly say that these are the only glasses I ride with.  Particularly if the windshield is off of my Road King.The killer feature with these glasses is the foam padding--if they fit your face, and they fit most people, the seal around your eye sockets is complete, so you eyes will never water on the road again.  At speed on the bike they will breathe adequately, but can get a little warm when walking around the biker rally.  But when riding they're so excellent that I don't even bring a pair of regular sunglasses with me.The impact protection is more than adequate.  I've taken a locust at 65 mph which glanced off the left side, and it hurt my skin around the impact more than anything else.These glasses do not scratch easily and that this price point can easily last you a riding season.  I keep two extra pair--clears and smoked--in my saddlebags for emergencies.  At $10 I can give them to biker friends who've lost their goggles once in a while and just say, have a nice day, you know?You need to periodically check the screws at the hinges after a few months.As an added bonus, they do not look bad at all. I have even been told they look pretty cool.  Every biker I have turned on to these sunglasses has ended up thanking me profusely. My future wife didn't like them because she's a little gal, and has a narrow face, but if you're a regular sized person, they will probably fit just fine. I'm a smallish guy and they fit my face fine, I've loaned them out to bigger fellows and likewise.If you ride a motorcycle with a skid lid or half helmet, at this price point, you owe it to yourself to try these.

reviewText: There are some costumes that look great, and then there are some in which the picture does do the product justice. I have gotten some costumes that seem like they are from the same company, but I may have been wrong about that.Be careful seeing the product picture as the picture looks better than the product. Let me explain more. First off, the outfit itself is not bad and fits pretty well. Some of the extras that come with it is what you are going to complain about. The wrist and shin guards are made of a thin styrofoam with painting for detail. They did the right thing by placing a thin plastic sheet to keep the items separated because some of the items would stick when you tried to take it out of the package. One of the main problems is the arm and leg guards don't have much velcro to work with. So if you don't have a lot of meat on your bones, it will feel a little loose. The mask is the biggest joke. It's nothing more than the front half of the mask with a rubber strap to put around the back of your head. (Yeah, it's a kids mask, not a full hooded mask that covers your entire head) So, when you order this, you might want to also order a black hood of some kind so it looks good. It does "not" come with a hood to go with the mask. Also, when you get the costume, make sure you air out the mask as it still has the stink of plastic/rubber on it. There are no air holes around the mouth area, so practice using the mask before you actually use it. The suit is basically a one piece outfit that you slip into. My only real complaint is the mask. I was seriously thinking that it was a full hooded mask, as the picture "seems" to show, but it's not. Overall, this is not a bad costume, just be ready for the surprises I mentioned. If you can, try to also see if you can order the "Sub-Zero Mask" that is sold separately.Warning = I got an X-Large and it fits perfectly for a person who is 5'6/175 lbs. So with this in mind, that means anyone who is 6 feet tall, you might want to order an XX-Large, and if you are under 5'4, you might want to order a Large. Ideally, this was meant for a fairly slender person. Please keep this in mind when you order this.
summary: Wow, this is not what I was expecting...

Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. They've even been used out of this world, having become standard issue on the Space Shuttle in 1990.

It kept my neck warm, but the fabric in the forehead and ear area was very thin, and I certainly felt the cold while running when it was below 25F. It's usually colder than that while skiing, plus you have the wind in your face, so I'm not sure how they came to their conclusion about it being great for skiing.The other reason I bought this was because they guaranteed your googles would not fog up while wearing it and working out. If it was just covering my mouth, the glasses did not fog, but when you're running in extreme cold (15F or below with the windchill), you really need to be able to cover both.The faults aside, it was very comfortable to wear and fit well in various configurations. If it wasn't too cold outside, and I didn't need it on my face, I could wear it like a hat and stick my ponytail through the face part in the back. I really liked the nice bright color it came in too, since I'm tired of all the black and gray winter clothes, and I like to  be highly visible when I'm running on the road.

title: TETON Sports Bookbag Backpack
description: All this for so little?  This book bag has features usually found on a pack twice the price.  Two main compartment are big enough for a laptop or the largest text or notebooks. reviewText: I ride transit daily to and from work and bought this to replace an old backpack which was starting to wear out.This is not a huge backpack, and I have larger ones I take to the grocery store for large loads but this more than adequately totes the daily junk I need to transport. I successfully managed to fit a large widescreen laptop in it but nothing any larger would be a decent fit. Hold a six pack and a few convenience items for that quick convenience store stop on the way home.There are two large main pockets which if combined would probably give you more capacity but it does a nice job of giving you a space for your newspaper in one while giving the cargo space for a laptop, light jacket or whatever else you need in the other. The front pocket has places for pens and you can organize aspirin, tissues or other daily need items in there without it getting terribly cluttered. There is one really small pocket on top of this which I have not found too much use for but might be handy for something (if you can fit your hand in there).The straps are very comfortable and most impressive about this bag. The suspension strap seems to help a bit with heavier loads but mostly I like the comfortable padding which has a breathable fabric to help keep you from getting sweaty under the straps which was often a problem for me with my old backpack.I would definitely recommend this over some of the more popular and well known bags such as JanSport. The cost is much less and the quality is excellent.----Update: February, 2011 one strap on this started to separate at the stitching. Consider though that this had two and a half years of daily use and I tend to load it up (both to capacity and with a lot of weight) when stopping at the store on my way home from work it's help up pretty well for an inexpensive backpack but it's now time to replace it. It's served me well.
summary: Great small backpack for day to day use

title: Spirit 20" Pirate Parrot
categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Novelty, Costumes & More', 'Costumes & Accessories', 'More Accessories']
description: Includes: Parrot prop Not included: Pirate costume, accessories
reviewText: So we looked at several shoulder parrots online and liked this the best for color and size.  When we got it we were still pleased, it is big enough (18 inches long) for an adult, colorful and very light weight (under 4 ounces), a styrofoam core, lots of feathers.  Head, eyes and beak are realistic and we liked how the head is turned.  But we were puzzled by how to fasten it on my shoulder.  It comes with a long white elastic strap fastened between the two feet.  After various attempts, this elastic band still showed, the bird did not stay upright and we finally succeeded in pulling out both of the bird's feet!  So we carefully cut the elastic off the feet and reglued them into the body with Elmer's glue.  When they had dried, we came up with the answer for mounting this bird.  We cut a piece of chopstick to fit through the hole in the bird's feet.  Then we simply took a binder clip and went up beneath the shirt fabric and clipped on the stick between the bird's feet.  We took another small clip and clipped the long tail down to the shirt in back.  The bird still wanted to slide toward my arm as my shirt was loose fabric, so we took a shoestring and tied it to one foot and loosly around my neck. That kept it right in position.  This looks like a leash like you would have with a real bird, and you can't see the binder clip under the shirt. You probably wouldn't need the leash if you had stiffer or tighter fabric with your shirt or blouse. You may have another way to fasten the bird on your shoulder, but this worked for us and we got through a long day at a pirate festival just fine and could freely use our arms to play an instrument.  We love this bird and will use him again next year, or sooner if the occasion allows! We had many nice comments on the bird.  Enjoy!
summary: Nice parrot, takes some thought to mount on shoulder

title: Croakies Premium Leather Cord Eyewear Retainer
description: The Croakies Premium Leather Cord Eyewear Retainer is made of a genuine, full grain round leather cord, and are great for apres-sport activities when a bit of fashion is called for. The ends tightly grip your glasses frames, so while you may lose yourself in your favorite activity, your glasses will remain securely strapped to your head.About CroakiesIn 1977, a local ski patrolman from Jackson Hole Mountain Resort in Wyoming came up with an idea for an eyewear retainer that would grip his shades through all kinds of alpine adventures. Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. They've even been used out of this world, having become standard issue on the Space Shuttle in 1990.

description: Sno-Seal Original Beeswax Waterproofing protects leather from rain, sun, snow, and salt. The beeswax formula dries to a solid wax that "stays put" in the surface of the leather so it lasts longer.  Our competitors' greases, oil, and animal products are able to migrate through the leather till they clog all the pores. These waterproofing products fill the natural spaces that are supposed to absorb perspiration and insulate.  In addition, animal fats weaken and rot leather. The tannery worked hard to remove the fats and preserve the leather, so it's hard to imagine why you'd put it back on.  Sno-Seal will help you feel more comfortable in Gore-Tex fabric lined boots because it allows the Gore-Tex-absorbed perspiration to escape out of the leather.  And not only will Sno-Seal keep you warm and dry, it'll also help you from getting tired. A typical leather boot can soak up to a pound of water. That means you lift an additional 2,212 lbs. to walk one mile. Sno-Seal keeps the whole boot dry, warm and light.
reviewText: I bought Sno Seal out of the recommendation of my best friend.  He used it on a pair of boots he wore and always raved about how amazing the stuff was at waterproofing the leather and keeping his feet dry.  Living in Oregon,  wet feet in the winter is hard to avoid.  I had just accepted this as a price for living where I did.But I decided to take his advice and use Sno-Seal.  And I have to say,  I am more than amazed.  It is an incredibly effective product.  It is super easy to apply.  Youll want to get whatever leather you are waterproofing nice and warm ( I used a spaceheater).  Then you just keep rubbing the wax into the leather until no more can be absorbed.  Thats it.NOW, there is a huge disclaimer that I feel the bottle doesnt truly give justice.  This will drastically change the color of the leather.  I have a pair of Clarks that were tan.  Sno-Seal turned them a shade of dark brown. I knew this was going to happen after seeing my roommates shoes (the color change was actually half the reason I bought the stuff; it gives incredible depth and character to the leather that is very appealing).  IF YOU USE THIS ON LIGHT LEATHER,  IT WILL DARKEN IT BY A LARGE MARGIN.  Just be aware of that and spot test if you are unsure of it.But that being said,  this stuff works great.  Water beads off my boots now and my feet are staying dry in conditions that would otherwise leave me soaked.  Great price, easy to apply, and will lengthen the life of your leather products by a huge amount.  Couldnt recommend this stuff more!

Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. They've even been used out of this world, having become standard issue on the Space Shuttle in 1990.

title: Medieval Chain Mail Shirt and Coif Armor Set (Full Size) Fit upto 3XL Long Shirt
description:
The wearing of chain mail has been an effective means of protection in combat and war of countries. Its use dates back to the Creeks and early Roman empire where warriors and legionnaires donned metal plate. The medieval era knights and most remembered for their elaborate chain mail in different designs. the period of chain mail armor runs from about the early 1300's to about the mid to late 1500's.

You are bidding a high quality Chain Mail shirt and coif set. Zinc plated steel construction. Weights 32 pounds. Will fit up to 48" chest. 17" from underarm to wrist, 34" from top of shoulder to thigh. 18 gauge and 1/4" ring size.
reviewText: I am happy to say not a single link was missing & both coif & shirt are very well made! It fits me like a glove but I am 5 foot 7 inches tall. I would think that a big man would have some issues, I have a 48 inch chest & the shirt is tight on me & only hangs down to groin level much like a large T-shirt. I feel very lucky as both coif & shirt fit me well enough & a 48inch chest is stretching the chainmail. Also beware if you have long hair when you put these on make sure your hair is contained, completely covered!!! I was fortunate enough to foresee the potential & tucked all five of my braids inside a wool winter cap! When I took off the chain mail it did snag my hat. If I would have put the chain mail coif or shirt on without covering my hair I would now have 10+ lbs of beautiful chainmail entangling my locks!!! Yes it would have been funny but I am guessing it would have hurt quite a bit, as well as involving a long yoga like grappling match trying to free my hair from the chainmail! Also I have read reviews where people had difficulties removing their chainmail. The key to this is stay relaxed & let gravity do the majority of the work for you, let it slide off DO NOT try & put your arms inside the shirt!!!!!!!! The next time I put my chainmail on I will use a tight weaved cotton head bandana instead of a knit wool hat. After trying it on & taking it off it is still intact with no missing links. Handle your chainmail gently & I don't think you will have any problems. I am going to see if it is possible to rivet the links shut If I can it will triple the value of this already nice costume set! As far as 3XL I don't think so unless this chainmail can really stretch because I am on the short side of the spectrum & it fits me tightly I was anticipating it would hang to mid thigh but it barely hangs to the groin & is tight in the chest so big men beware! My daughter & her boyfriend tried it on & it does come down to their thighs when they say up to 48 inch chest they mean it! Any bigger & you will have to pass on this deal.
summary: Very well made for the price!!!

reviewerName: w i l l i a m
reviewText: I have used Fiebings and Angelus leather dyes in black (and Angelus' suede dye) and neither of them dyed to a true black - they both are penetrating dyes that seep into and darken the leather but will not give you a TRUE black.  They leave a metallic/bronze sheen on the leather which is horrifying when you don't know how to fix it.  TARRAGO self shine dye in black will go over these dyes finishing the leather in a true black.  If you're dyeing colored leather to black you will probably need the penetrating dye and tarrago to do the job, but if you're touching up black shoes you will only need the tarrago dye.  Buffing the leather with mink oil after the leather has dried will also help eliminate any streaks or unevenness in the dye while moisturizing the leather.
summary: Only dye I have found that dyes to a true black.

reviewText: I didn't really need another pair of sunglasses, but I grabbed a pair of these because I found them cheap and they were polarized (I love Wiley X glasses, but I never tried their polarized glasses before). I suppose it should not come as much of a surprise, they are the best polarized glasses I've ever seen. The frames are typical Wiley X grilamide nylon, so they're also quite good (very similar to my old Xcesses). The style is full frame wraparound, they fit my face well, and don't let much light in around the sides, which I also really like. And yes, I think they look great as well. Is there anything that could be improved? Well I still prefer the half frame, and the shield to the full frame. My Saints and my Sabers both breathe much better, and stay cleaner if I'm running around sweating a lot. On the other hand, the polarized lenses are even better than either the plain Smoke lenses (my Sabers) or the Silver Flash Smoke lenses (My Saints), so I think I've got a new primary pair of driving glasses here. For other people, these would be a great choice for activities where the definition provided by polarized glasses is an advantage (fishing, golfing ect).  A quick glance at the time I'm writing this review indicates these Mojos are competitive with the cheapest Costa Del Mar glasses you can get her on Amazon and much cheaper than the least expensive Maui Jim glasses or polarized Oakleys, and those would constitute what I'd call the "Big 3" of high end sporting sunglasses. Wiley X are a great alternative to all of the above, and my personal favorite brand. These Mojos fill another niche I didn't even know I needed, and I can recommend them highly, though my purchase was an easier decision than you have here because I lucked out and got a better price (this one is still reasonable though as its still half the MSRP)
summary: Wiley Silver Flash Polarized Lens is the best I've ever seen

reviewText: I live in the tropics and the sun blazes relentlessly day in and day out. So I have to wear head protection and the Bora Bora Booney is a smart and comfy way to keep skin on my bean. It packs easily, compressing into almost nothing. As far as hats go, it's cooler than average due to the mesh ventilation and lightweight fabric, and certainly cooler than my old cotton bucket and ball caps. But not as cool as myColumbia Men's Coolhead Ball Cap III (Omni-Freeze ZERO).It's engineered as a sunhat and the dense weave fabric and large brim provide excellent protection, besting any bucket or ball cap. No sign of burn on my noggin even after a day in the sun. Of course, should you get caught in a tropical downpour, the mesh ventilation windows leak, so not a rain hat. The adjustable chin strap keeps it from blowing away in mild trade wind but the brim is too large and floppy for heavy wind or typical ocean boat trips. I'm a photographer and the Booney's brim, although large, easily flexes out of the way when I shoot verticals with a DSLR. It fact, the Booney makes a fine lens shade! Alas, the brim is too floppy to stay if folded up--Australian explorer look--and lacks a snap to lock it in place.Hat size is adjustable via drawstring. At default the hat is too large for my size 7.25 bean. A slight tug of the drawstring and the clip locks on my hat size and stays put. Simple but effective.Construction quality is excellent: not a loose thread, nylon fabric is of good quality and it feels and looks durable. It does rock the safari look something fierce, so it that isn't your thing, check out Columbia's Omni-Shade buckets or ball caps. However, I dig it and pair it with a Columbia Omni-Shade shirt most of the time.This fair weather sun hat is wonderful for protecting my noggin and upper face during hiking, beach and gardening. It's not designed for strong wind or rain. Finally, the big side benefit I'm enjoying is not having to use so much darn sun screen!
summary: Comfy, protective & rocks the safari look somethin' fierce!

reviewText: This was a great purchase! I snowboard and I don't perspire very much, like some of the reviewers, but, nevertheless, my boot liners do need to be dried after a day on the slopes. That's fine if I just went up for a day. I just pull the liners out and let the boots & liners air dry. But when I go for several days at a time, that can be a hassle, or you wind up worried that air-drying wasn't enough. And you've also got gloves and a helmut and other stuff that needs drying. This is the solution to the problem. It's small enough that it's portable. You can throw it into the car if you're going up to the mountains for a few days (I kept the box for this purpose). Note that this MAY be smaller or more delicately-built than you might expect it to be; it's not the sturdiest thing in the world. So, it may need to be a little more careful with this than with some products. You certainly can't throw it into the trunk with the boots and boards and stuff. Needs to be in a box where it won't rattle around or get creamed by some other gear. The cord wraps around the bottom, which is nice for storage. Doesn't retract or anything, tho. The controls are easy to use, and the timer's nice so that it turns off automatically. If you have a big family, you might want to get two. Things dry fairly fast, but for a family of four, say, you'd have to be pretty religious about timing the first person's gear, taking it off when done, putting the second person's gear on, taking it off when done, etc.

description: This shoe bag protects clothing from shoes in your suitcase, with these Travel Shoe Bags. reviewText: Search for Cosmos Shoe Bag to see the color variations you can get for this perfectly sized 17.25” x 13.5” shoe bag.  I got the four white bags, which as I write this, is now out of stock.  Other color options are all black or two white and two black.  The bags are large enough to serve well as dirty laundry bags when traveling or as a damp towel and bathing suit container when returning from the gym.  The material is tightly woven but not waterproof.  The bags are well made; the fabric is strong and smooth.  More important, and not pointed out in the description is that each of the bags I received has a cord clamp (squeeze-to-release-type).  That makes closing the bag supremely easy compared to the other bags I ordered at the same time, none of which came with a cord lock.  If you buy clamps separately for the others, which will add about $1 per bag to the cost and will necessitate time lost untying the knots and threading the clamps.  Further, many clamps on the market have weak springs and may not work well (see clamp reviews).  The clamps that came with the Cosmos bags hold.I use a size 12 men’s running shoe, and a pair nicely fit in this bag.  A bulky pair of casual shoes also fits well.  If you need bags for a size 10 men’s shoe or smaller, the nominal 15” bags should serve OK, especially the "FashionBoutique high quality waterproof Nylon shoe bags- Set of 4 (Multicolor)"  which gives you color coding.  The "Nylon Travel Shoe Bags Set of 3"  is serviceable, much cheaper, slightly smaller, and made of a much rougher but serviceable fabric.  Either of the smaller bags can hold my shoes, but with an open hole on one end of about 4’ to 5” diameter and requiring a force fit into the bag, which is not as wide as the Cosmos.Initially this review was written for the white bags, but I am posting it as well for the same sized all black and half black half white options which I have no doubt are of the same construction.  The cautious buyer might want to contact the seller directly (follow Amazon’s links) to verify that the other colors come with the cord locks, since no pictures or description for any color of the Cosmos bags said such clamps were included.Black bag addendum: I note that one reviewer said that cord locks came with the black bags.

reviewText: This dress was exactly what we wanted - something that looked a bit like Rapunzel's dress from the Disney movie, but would be unique (since there were undoubted a gazillion other 'Rapunzels' for Halloween in 2011), higher quality than the Disney dresses on the racks at Target, and might spark more creative play than a dress that was clearly intended to be "the" Rapunzel dress. I haven't seen any rips, tears, or loose stitching.  It's not a super-heavy cloth (not at this price!), and the 'crown' is a bit hard to keep on - but she loves it and has a lot of fun wearing it.  She'll still put it on first thing in the morning and wear it all day from time to time, even.  For the price we were willing to pay, this is just what we wanted and hoped for.Our daughter was five years old, just starting to wear size 6, and this (the Medium size) had a bit of extra room for her to grow in and for her to wear warm clothing under when trick-or-treating.  I think we might have needed to pin up the skirts, which are on the long side, just for Halloween, so that she could safely climb lots of stairs to front doors in the dark.  The skirts were fine for at-home play, though, even with our own staircase. description: The Kirkland Signature Men's T-Shirts combine our heavyweight combed cotton fabric with reinforced seams and tagless labels to produce one of the most durable and comfortable T-shirts you've ever worn. It's just the kind of quality you expect from Kirkland Signature.
reviewText: What would inspire a guy who bought 6 white undershirts at a warehouse club to go onto Amazon and write a review?  If you had told me I would do this after buying the shirts, I would have called you crazy.  But here I am, and this is going to be one of the most glowing reviews I have ever written.First of all, for those of you who have not been bitten by the Costco bug, you have not yet lived.  Sure, Amazon is the ultimate online experience, and that'll always be my first stop for just about anything.  But if you are looking for a treasure hunt in a good ol' brick and mortar store, you cannot beat Costco.  It puts Sam's Club to shame for fun factor and quality of merchandise, including both brand names and the house brand--Kirkland Signature.  Never hesitate for a moment when given the choice of a Kirkland Signature over a national brand.  This is Costco.  You are not shopping the grocery store, Target, or some other retailer where private label means second rate.  Rather, it means BUY ME, I AM BETTER THAN THE NATIONAL BRAND--A TRUE VALUE THAT CANNOT BE BEATEN.And so begins the story of my first experience with these exquisite undershirts.  Having long been a fan of Kirkland Signature products, I knew they would be good, but NEVER did I think I would be so inspired by an undershirt.  By this time, you are thinking I am a few cards short of a full deck.  Sure, think what you want.  You haven't experienced these T-shirts.  So, maybe I should tell you what makes them so great:+ Thick & Luxurious: The difference here is like the difference between a cheap bath towel and one of those really thick, soft, heavy bath towels that you usually only find in expensive hotels.  Really, these undershirts are unmistakably superior, and you'll know it from the moment you touch the cotton.  Some of you pansies are thinking, "Oh, I would sweat in those." They are cotton, I say.  They breathe.  Not to worry.+ Tight Weave: Those ordinary undershirts (Hanes, Fruit of the Loom, whatever) are all the same.  They are cheap, lightweight fabric that stretches terribly.  Just try to stretch one of these undershirts.  You'll instantly know that these shirts are cut from a different cloth, literally.+ Fitted Shape: If you have a pot belly or wear a man bra, don't buy these undershirts, as they are made for the rest of us--those whose proportions more closely resemble a human being than a bowling pin.  I appreciate a shirt that isn't made to fit either me or Fred Flintstone.+ Long Length: Cheapo undershirts sell "Tall" versions of their shirts for guys that don't want their shirts coming untucked.  Kirkland Signature gives everybody a longer shirt, because WHO THE HECK WANTS HIS SHIRT COMING UNTUCKED?!?  This is a benefit we should all enjoy, and you will if you buy this shirt.+ Value: My price in store was lower than what I see online, but I would pay this price without batting an eye, if I could not find these in my local Costco.  They are one of those products that is just SO MUCH BETTER than anything else that they are worth a few extra bucks.+ Preshrunk: Mine fit perfectly right out of the package.  Since then, they have been washed and dried several times, and they still fit perfectly.+ Tagless: OK, so the cheap undershirts do this now, too, but it is still worth mentioning that Kirkland Signature has it right with no scratchy tags.I am so impressed with these shirts that my wheels have been turning ever since I put on the first one.  What else could I do with them?  Could I dye them and wear them as regular casual shirts?  Could I embroider them for a customized style?  Could I screen print them?  Could I start my own t-shirt company and use these shirts as the raw material for so many great creative expressions?  The answer to these questions is all YES!Hats off to Kirkland Signature for making such an inspirational undershirt.  Yes, inspirational undershirt.  It's that good.

reviewText: I bought these glasses because I wanted something optically correct (meaning that things don't change shape and/or size when one views them through the lenses), something with a full coverage and a good history. These glasses fit the bill. I use them for flying almost 6x a week and they do a great job of cutting down on the brightest spots while increasing the dynamic range of the light emitted (so the contrast is higher while not being painfully bright). They are durable as well. My only negative is the style, which is unavoidable if you want minimum distortion (if you bend lenses it's much harder to produce a flat image). They are on the heavy side, but I consider that "durable" instead of a negative.
