reviewText: Let me start this review by saying the first one I bought was broken right out of the box. I plugged it in and the fan made a couple of clicking noises, then it got hot and started smoking. I quickly unplugged it and boxed it back up. Amazon was fantastic with the exchange. They had the replacement package in the mail the next morning before I ever even got to the UPS store to get the defective one sent out. In fact, the new one arrived at my house the same day that I sent out the defective one. And, of course, Amazon covered all shipping. Well done Amazon.I am very happy with this unit. I can't believe how quickly it dries out shoes, boots, and gloves. No more hanging these in front of a fan or placing them over a vent and waiting an eternity for them to dry. This has also done wonders for getting rid of foot stink of shoes and boots. I have a pair of motorcycle boots that have seen about 30,000 miles of hard use. I was spraying them with foot spray and Febreze nearly daily to cover up the stink. After a couple of days of putting them on this dryer, the smell is completely gone! The same can be said of my two boys' stinky soccer shoes... Smell completely gone.It is fan driven, so it is a little bit noisy (very slight noise, definitely not a complaint), but it moves a fair amount of air. When the heat setting is selected, the air that comes out is warm, not hot, so it should be safe for any shoe or boot I would imagine.I've used it on some fairly tall dual sport motorcycle boots (about 13.5" tall) and they fit with about a half an inch to spare. If your boots are much taller than this, I'd consider getting the extensions. I've also used this with gloves and it does a fantastic job of drying them as well. I wouldn't bother with the glove attachments... No need to fix what isn't broken!My only complaints with this unit involve the timer dial. You can set it at 240 minutes (4 hrs) max. I'd like to have the option to just turn it on and have it run all night. So far, everything I've put in it has dried within the 4 hours... However, it would be nice to have the choice to leave it longer without having to reset the timer. Also, once the timer runs down to '0' if you turn the knob to increase the time nothing will happen. You have to first twist it the opposite way (normally to decrease time) and it will then set it to the maximum time and then quickly decrease it. You then must twist it to increase the time. This little quirk is no big deal at all; just a minor annoyance really. However, I figured it was worth mentioning.I would definitely recommend this product to others.

title: Think Tank Airport International V 2.0
description: TheThinkTank Airport International rolling camera caseis thoughtfully designed for the international traveler to take the maximum amount of gear possible as legal carry-on baggage. reviewText: Okay, I don't know what's going on here because I have a Think Tank backpack and think the quality is top shelf.  This $329 rolling camera bag body looks great and is very well built as I would expect from a Think Tank.  However, when I extended the handle, I was, let's just say, shocked to see how poor the quality was.  I've owned a number of rolling bags in my life and this was literally the flimsiest, most rickety handle I have yet to see on a rolling bag, of any brand or price!I was really disappointed to see this because this bag is designed to house a 500mm lens, a 70-200mm and a couple of bodies.  So, we're talking about gear valued in the neighborhood of $12,000 to $15,000 range? (depending on the bodies) and weighing in at least 17 lbs plus the 14 lbs of the bag.  W-H-O in their right might would transport $15,000 worth of gear with a handle that feels like it's about to give out from the moment it's taken out of the box?  Not me, that's for sure.  I'm so surprised by the inferior quality that I'm going to call Think Tank directly and inquire.  I just don't want to believe that this is what they call quality. How can you product a 5 star bag then put a .25 star quality handle on it?I want to try another bag because it's construction and size is exactly what I need so if I just got a lemon, I will definitely post another review.***UPDATED REVIEW JANUARY 11, 2010***Okay, here's the deal.  I went to a local camera shop that carried the bag and gave a try.  The handle felt sturdier than the one I got from Norman Camera so I decided to call Think Tank Photo and ask them about my issue.  The rep I spoke to told me that although I was not the first to complain about the handle, he also assured me that he had never seen one come back because the handle broke so I decided to give this bag another try, this time Adorama, I company I know and trust.Guess what?  The handle is still not rock solid but it's DEFINITELY better! AND this time it can lock at second tier so that shorter people can comfortably roll the bag too.  I'm really glad I gave it another try so I've increased my rating from 3 stars to 4 stars.  If Think Tank would make the handle that didn't shake I would give it 10 stars because like I said from the start, these guys know how to make camera bags.Think Tank and Adorama also know how to talk to their customers, unlike Norman Camera because instead of using good customer service skills and trying to make an  unhappy customer feel better about their shopping experience, I got an email from those guys calling my review "a rant."  I was in the customer service business for years, that's NOT what you do when you've got an unhappy customer on your hands because in our case, repeat business was the name of the game.Here's my closing advice:The bag is good if you need to carry 500mm, a 70-200mm, a wide angle, and a couple of bodies internationally and BUY THE BAG DIRECTLY FROM AMAZON OR ADORAMA.I hope I've helped somebody out there.

reviewText: These are fantastic! You can stop reading and just buy a pair or two or more, and give them as gifts as I do. They are literally life-savers on the slick ice. I've bought these for family members, friends, and others have bought them after hearing me rave about them. I don't go outside without them in slick weather.You just slip them over your shoes or boots, as close to the door as possible, because you don't want to walk with them inside. They might damage the floor and they are slick to walk on inside. Great outside!My neighbor across the street was shocked when I rang his doorbell in a huge ice storm, to bring his mail to him. He said, "How did you do that? There is no way anyone could make it up that steep driveway." I showed him the Yaktrax and he said, "If that's what did it, I'm buying some" and he did. Now he brings my mail when we have ice and snow.Usually we have more ice than snow, and these work really well with the kinds of ice storms we have. Then we had a snow storm, and they worked equally well. Finally, we had a different kind of snow, which packed into the Yaktrax. They still worked, but the snow was so fine, I guess, and there was so much of it, that it was still treacherous walking out there.All-in-all, I think everyone should have these if you have snow and ice in winter.I've learned to put these on when I'm right by the door with something to hold onto. They are slick to walk on inside. They won't do your floor any good either.EDITED years after getting my first pair. I've given away half a dozen now. I don't know how I made it without them. Our weather has been crazy with icy winters. Before getting these I remember some really dangerous situations. These are literally life-savers in my opinion. reviewText: I got the CD-2800 with the cleaning cloth and gem cleaner combo. The cleaner has a plastic basket inside to hold small items. Set-up and use is amazingly easy. Before first use, I rinsed the inside (which is made of stainless steel) and the basket.Cleaning your items is as simple as adding tap water, putting your item in and pressing the on button. After that, the cleaner just buzzes for about 3 minutes, then it's done.I experimented with this quite a bit and I found the best combination is warm water with a few drops of regular washing detergent. I had varying success with eye glasses. Grime that was pretty recent was easy to dislodge but grime that was years old from old glasses was difficult to get rid of. Gold that was dull became bright and shiny. categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Novelty, Costumes & More', 'Watch Accessories', 'Repair Tools & Kits']
description: All the tools you will need to open almost any type watch case for battery replacement. Comes in a protective tool roll for easy storage.
reviewText: I have been getting charged for changing batteries, changing links quite excessively as of late and I figured, why not do it myself.Of course, as a beginner, I wasn't sure which tools to buy (even after reading conflicting reviews), so I purchased the 16-piece SE set, the SE watch case tool with adapters and this 10 piece set.Unlike the others which are made in China, this one is made in India.I.  TOOLSThe tools in this Battery Replacement set are:- Two mini-screwdrivers- Watch Case Opener (horizontal and not the usually two-three tip tool with adapter)- Seiko case remover- Plastic tweezer- Non-Magnetic Tweezer- Dust Brush- KnifeII.  Removing Watch Case BackAnd this is probably the tool that I actually have had more success in removing case-backs with a hole on the caseback and that is using the watch tool remover that came with this set.  It was easy to use and it's funny that a few jewelers were unable to open the case with their watch case opener (the blue object in picture), so I was glad to see that this thing came in handy.I used the screwdrivers from this set the most than what I have in my 16-piece as it looks more sturdy.I liked how it came with the brush, because if you are opening older watches, you'll notice crumbs or dirt that could have gotten inside and so the brush comes in handy.The knife looked like I can cut myself easy with it, so I preferred to use the knife case opener for older vintage watches to remove the case back.  These casebacks have no holes or divots but by putting your knife to an angle near the lugs, these type of cases then remove easily with the knife.I also look at the Seiko opener and plastic and non-magnetic tweezers as great tool additions to this set.III.  PRICEFor those who want to change batteries, it's a pretty great deal for under $10.IV.  OVERALLThere were tools that came in handy and were very useful for several watches that my 16-piece set was unable to open.  I do recommend this set as an addition to the 16-piece set but if you are looking to remove case-backs, the blue object on its own is $4 so, it's worth owning as I found it easier to remove the case for some watches.  The Brush is also a nifty addition and literally, you're getting quite a bit for this cheap set.Now knowing what I do know after buy three SE products, if you are going to be changing batteries on quartz watches and also removing casebacks and links, I recommend the 16-piece SE set.  But because this 10-piece comes with items with each selling for $3.99-$4.99 each, it's a worth addition to your 16-piece watch fixing set as it has beneficial tools such as the sturdier mini-screwdrivers the brush and most importantly the case removing tools.  It's also not a bad idea just in case you have problems or you lose a tool, you can look to these extra tools as a backup to your pre-existing tool set.But if you need to purchase one, this one is great for removing case-backs and for changing batteries.  It's very affordable... but once again, you may find the SE 16-piece more suitable for you. Especially if you want to start removing your own links.  And for batteries, it may not remove all cases and even the 16-bit set may be ineffective for challenging watches, so a SE watch case tool with several adapters may be what you need.But once again, for the price of this 10-piece set and how much the items inside it cost quite a bit if sold piece-by-piece.  It's a steal!  Definitely recommended!
summary: Comes with the basics to open a case back but I recommend this as an addition to the 16-piece set.

title: Lowepro LP36407-PAM Pro Messenger 180 AW Backpack (Slate Grey)
description: When your gear feels right, your work goes more smoothly. The Pro Messenger AW - a soft-sided bag that fits pro-sized gear - was designed with this idea in mind.
reviewText: For this review I'll get straight to the point without the blah, blah or blah.Pros:1. Bag looks aesthetically pleasing in a nice Army green colour2. It is very well padded3. Has two straps - one for over the shoulder, and one hand strap4. Lots of internal pockets for gear5. Fancy front Flexflap design with Velcro and magnets provides your choice of secure or easy access, or full working access (aka wide open)6. Rear pocket can be zipped to provide storage space, or unzipped to fit over the extended handle of your rolling suitcase for easy mobility.7. Comes with all weather cover stowed in the bottom8. Can fit a DSLR fitted with a 70-200mm f/2.8 lens, plus an external flash, plus two smaller lenses in the main compartment.9. Can fit a second camera body or point and shoot in front pocket.10.  Two external side pockets can possibly hold a small water bottle each.Cons:1. It's bigger and more clunky than it looks in the photos2. While it can work as a gear bag for an event, it is too heavy (when fully stocked) for long walks, or everyday toting.3. Most of the weight comes from the shoulder strap and the shoulder pad, (which is much too bulky) and unfortunately neither is removable.4. The only access is through the top, so it is difficult to access gear at the bottom of the bag, or fix the internal padding correctly.  Unzipping all the way down for front access would have been a plus.5. No straps for a tripod or monopod (not a big thing if you're using it for street or urban photography, but like I said, it's heavy for a day tote, and you may be using it for events)This may look great on a big guy, but would be a bit overwhelming for a smaller framed person, especially if you have other gear to carry. It will however keep your gear safe and dry.I use this for small weddings, stage shows or school events, where I can put in down in a corner until I'm ready to pack up.  I definitely wouldn't want to walk around with it on my shoulder all day.And so the search for the perfect camera bag goes on.Amanda Richards, August 15, 2013

description: Unlike smooth leather, which can look great distressed and beat up, suede and nubuck leather just looks old and tired. On suede and sheepskin use the brass bristles on the Suede Brush to remove surface dirt. On Nubuck and Textiles use the rubber bristles on the Suede Brush. Nubuck and Textiles are durable but usually not as thick as suede. Next, use the side fan on the brush to remove dirt and debris from tight spots. Pedag makes waterproofers are ideal for all leathers and textiles, but other manufacturers make suitable waterproofers too. description: Very easy to use and includes instructions. Sealed box contains six (6) bottles test solution; each bottle contains 1/2 fluid oz (0.5 fl oz) test acid. reviewText: I have a large variety of golden items that have ended up in my jewelry box over the years. A lot of it was hand-me-downs from my mother, and a lot of it does not fit me anymore, or is not to my taste. I know that these items have a large value, but I was at a loss as to figure out exactly what each item is worth. At first, I thought this kit would provide what I wanted, but the more I thought about it, I realized that I needed other things and that a lot of the things in this kit are unnecessary. Here is what I ended up ordering in order to evaluate my rings and necklaces:Large Stone 4.25"x2"Gold Testing Solutions Kit 10k 14k 18k 22k Silver Platinum Scratch StoneAmerican Weigh Signature Series Black Digital Pocket Scale, 1000 by 0.1 gramsSE 30X Illuminated Jewelers Loupe100 Gram Chrome Scale Calibration Weight50-Gram Chrome Scale Calibration WeightRing Mandrel Finger Sizer Gauges Find Exact Size RingsCarson Z-Pix 34-168x Digital Zoom MicroscopeThis whole lot cost me a little over $50, and will provide me with the exact tools that I need for evaluating my gold rings and necklaces. In addition, I figured out how to estimate the size and value of the stones in my rings. I am not talking about diamonds, I am talking about finding the carat value of gemstones that are set in rings that cannot be dislodged. Get yourself a six-inch ruler (SE Ruler 6" - Double Sided - S.A.E/MM (2 Pack)) that is finely divided into millimeters, and measure to your best guess the dimensions of your gems. Then, go to[...]and enter your values. You will get your results in carats, and you can subtract the weight of your gemstones from the weight of the ring in order to estimate the amount of gold in your jewelry.I have not yet received the kit of this review, but I plan to return it when it arrives.

reviewText: I bought a Saucony ViziPro vest very similar to this a little over a year ago. Being seen by motorists in dark and low-light conditions was important to me.Bottom line, this vest makes you unbelievably (almost ridiculously) visible at night and in low-light conditions. It could literally save your life.This vest is far superior to most reflective running clothing or other reflective accessories. Most gear has at least a little reflective material on it, almost as an afterthought -- a stripe here, a Swoosh there -- but you really have to be looking for the runner to see it in your headlights. The reflective vests and ankle bands work pretty well, but only when it's in your headlights, and its visibility diminishes considerably as dawn approaches -- and you don't see it at all if you don't have your headlights on, which happens too often.This ViziPro Orange, on the other hand, screams out to motorists "LOOK OUT" in any lighting conditions. Look up "Saucony ViziPro" on YouTube, and you'll begin to see what I mean. You'll stick out like a sore thumb when you're wearing this vest -- which is exactly what you want to do.
summary: My most important piece of gear.

title: Croakies Premium Leather Cord Eyewear Retainer
description: The Croakies Premium Leather Cord Eyewear Retainer is made of a genuine, full grain round leather cord, and are great for apres-sport activities when a bit of fashion is called for. The ends tightly grip your glasses frames, so while you may lose yourself in your favorite activity, your glasses will remain securely strapped to your head.About CroakiesIn 1977, a local ski patrolman from Jackson Hole Mountain Resort in Wyoming came up with an idea for an eyewear retainer that would grip his shades through all kinds of alpine adventures. Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. They've even been used out of this world, having become standard issue on the Space Shuttle in 1990.
reviewText: This is a nice clean style' neither masculine or feminine. Utilitarian I would say..or just smart. He likes his grandpa's guitars, so it was important that a toy guitar for him had strings on it. He likes to pluck the strings, and hit the buttons - and he didn't even notice any of the other toys after we opened this one. It has been a couple months, and he still plays with it all the time - he dances and rocks back and forth like he his having the best time of his life. He hugs it. We haven't had to change the batteries yet.The songs aren't irritating (no peppy voices), it has two volume levels, and it lights up in an attractive/cool manner.I let him play around with the keyboard version in the store, and I think it would be as good as the guitar.The only negative thing I can think of, is that the sticker is getting grungy looking. It doesn't detract from the enjoyment of the toy, so it really isn't a big deal.

description: 203457 Features: For breathable waterproofing, the polyurethane coating doubled with silk protein delivers soft and dry comfort next to skin Give yourself a bit of extra move and stretch room in the articulated knees that simply won't hinder your stride For a sure fit over any number of layers, the elastic waistband, adjustable belt, and front fly all give you a bit of flexibility Nine-inch Velcro ankle closures seal out the cold and wet and fit easily over boots Specifications:
reviewText: I like these pants. The fit is good around the waist with an elastic waist and button/fly combo, except it's a bit too long in length for me. If you cinch them up with the velcro on the bottom, they puff out right above the ankle. This gives you the appearance of "hammer pants" from yesteryear. Then again, I'm 5'4'' and have issues finding pants that fit regardless of maker. Usually I would just hem them, but the way these are designed it doesn't seem to be possible what with the velcro clasps and all.These are made with the ConduitSilk material, which judging from my other Conduit pieces, should feel comfortable and wick sweat away with ease. These pants are no doubt completely waterproof and they are windproof, as I tested out today in about 15mph gusts. I hate how they don't have pockets, as I keep reaching for them to place my hands in or to deposit my cell into, and they're not there.. If they even had a side-zip pocket on the leg that would have been better. I can't judge them on that though since they're really meant to be pullover rain pants for inclement weather while active. They are very light and do pack up quite small. I will have no issue packing these into a daypack or similar 18L pack with a ton of other items. Pack space taken up by these is minimal. They do make some noise while walking in them, as can be expected from a pant like this, but it's a bit louder than I expected. Other pairs of pants I own similar to this one don't make that much noise, though they did cost me about 2-3 times as much.I'm a pretty active hiker and backpacker/hiker/camper, I do hope this pieces' sole purpose isn't to keep you dry as you walk in a parking lot from your Subaru Outback into Whole Foods Market. It's for backtrail wet weather while active. The Conduit Epic Jacket didn't get such favorable reviews on Trailspace dot com, so let's hope these hold up a bit better.On an aside, I do already own the Epic Gloves and let me tell you, not a better waterproof glove for the price you'll find.We'll see how it well holds up on my ski trip this weekend, i'll post back my findings for sure on or around Jan. 17, 2012. So far, I've only given them a 3 because I haven't real-world tested them yet.
summary: Great packable rain pants with one caveat

reviewText: If you had a "good" Lowepro once, you already know that it is hard to get used to any other bag. The quality, design, and comfort of most Lowepro bags are just outstanding. The 70-300G lens fits in the center, even when attached to the camera, and you can use each side compartments for one long zoom lens; alternately, you can stack up two smaller lenses--on top of each other--in each side compartments. The front pocket also can hold a spare body. There are also lots of spaces for memory cards, filters, lens caps, and etc.Because of the size and style, I was tempted to get theLowepro Exchange Messenger Camera Bag (Gray), but most reviewers have mentioned lack of enough padding. I also consideredLowepro Classified 160 AW Shoulder Bag for DSLR and 1-2 Lenses (Black), but the height of that one is just too long. Overall, this Pro Messenger 180 AW bag is very well padded, has an adequate size, and provides secure space for your precious gear. It is not flashy, but it is noticeable on your shoulder. My only complaint is the price, and that is the reason for 1 star rate decrease. I cannot justify the price difference between this bag and the Lowepro backpack that I've got.

title: Bobster Bolt Sunglasses - Black/Smoke
description: Bobster Bolt Sunglasses       The clear lenses are ideal in flat, low-light conditions and reduce glare from headlightsMulti layered mirrored coatingshown on outside of lens to help eliminate glareProves 100% protection against UVA and UVB rays, and are made from shatter-resistant polycarbonate, reducing the threat of air debrisHydrophilic nose pads that actually grip better when they are moistIncludes a microfiber pouch for easy transport
reviewText: So, I already had a favorite brand of sunglasses, and that would be Wiley X (see my review of their Sabers), but my ultimate pair of Wileys would be the Saints with mirror smoke lens, those run close to $80, and there's a good chance I could hate myself forever if I dropped that kind of money on a pair of sunglasses. I decided to see if maybe I could find a different brand of glasses that could scratch my itch for a pair of Saints. On paper these Bobster Bolts have everything I could want:-100% UV protection-ANSI rated polycarbonate lenses-Scratch Resistant Coating-Polycarbonate used is optically correct-Grilamid Nylon frames-Wraparound frame style-"Smoke Gray" lens tint-Mirror Coated lens-Hydrophilic nose pads grip your face even better when wet-They even have an antifog coating (should also make the glasses easier to clean and less likely to smudge)But of course, no matter how good a pair of glasses sound, you won't really know how they ARE until you recieve them and wear them. In this case, the product is basically as good as it sounded on paper. First, let me note that not every pair of glasses that claims to have "decentered" or "distortion free" lenses is the same (for example the Rawlings glasses on this site that sell for $20-$30 utilize such lenses and are immediately and obviously inferior to a pair of Oakleys, Wiley X's, OR these Bobsters). The glasses work great in a wide variety of lighting conditions. They're very effective in bright sunlight, but still allow you enough light to see in most shadow conditions. The fit is excellent and very secure, yet still fairly comfortable (credit the nosepads, the fact that these glasses are light as a feather, and flexible temple pieces, grilamid isn't just tough, its also comfortable). Coverage and field of vision are both very good, though not as good as my Wiley X Xcess's or Sabers. That's due to the size of the glasses and the size of my head (these are listed in Bobster's catalog as "small" size, and apparently I don't have a small head.Anyway, at this point, you might be wondering why I only gave 4 stars? If I could I'd give 4 1/2, but to me they lose half a point because with the same tint listed as my Wiley X glasses (Grey Smoke), these glasses do NOT give quite the same neutral tint. I know, that's very nitpicky, and possibly a bit unfair (Bobster does specifically state the mirror coating will enhance contrast and brightness, but this specific lens is the nearest thing Bobster makes to my personal favorite, and I like my Wiley X's better)Anyway, aside from the fact that there's one company that makes glasses I like even better (two if you count Oakley, and someone would gave me a pair of grey tinted silver mirrored Flak Jackets for free no way I'll ever pay $150 for sunglasses), you'd be hard pressed to go wrong with these Bobster Bolts. Assuming you like the mirror tint on the outside (and I for one prefer it), I'd say they compare very favorably to Ray Ban's extremely popular RB4115 series, which are literally twice the price even on Amazon and list for nearly 3 times the price elsewhere. I've never owned said Ray Bans, but I've tried them a few times, and these Bobsters aren't just cheaper or more durable, their lenses are optically better, at least to my eyes. So these are a great pair of unisex glasses. Not all Wiley X's or all Bobsters are this cheap, but between the 2 companies, (plus maybe American Optical for classic Aviators) you can get pretty a really excellent pair of nearly any style of sunglasses for around $40.
summary: Excellent. Second only to Wiley X

title: Thule 2014 Perspektiv� Messenger Bag
description: The Perspektiv Messenger leads a double lifeuse it as a pure courier bag for your daily commute and on the weekends as a mini camera studio to snap pictures for your evolving album. A removable pod system provides a modular option for carrying just the essentials or to store your equipment for safekeeping.
reviewText: Firstly, the good stuff:- The shoulder strap is extremely comfortable.- The inside main section is quite roomy.- The insert is bright blue (as opposed to the typical black) making it easy to find small photographic items that are typically black.- There is a zipper that allows access to the main compartment without lifting the flap.  It even has a very nice ring pull that makes it easy to hold on to and open.  That is handy when you want to remove something without revealing the contents of your bag to everyone around you by lifting the flap.  (more on that later)Now, the not-so-good stuff:- There is no way to hook additional items to the outside of this bag.  For example, my "go-to" daily messenger bag is aTenba 638-235 Large Engraveable Messenger Bag.  It has fittings on the outside where I can hang holders for additional lenses, a water bottle, or a travel mug.- Remember that comfortable strap and convenient top zipper?  When the bag with this permanently attached strap is designed to be carried "messenger bag style" which is across your back.  That makes it possible for a bad person to use the easily accessed zipper to open your bag and remove things.- The inside, while roomy, can really only accommodate your camera with attached lens plus two additional items (two lenses or one lens and one flash).- There is little accommodation for accessories and what there is could have been better though out.  If you like having small compartments to hold different things look elsewhere.  I also found it interesting that the flap with pockets to hold memory cards (primarily SD cards) folds down.  While it's unlikely that the cards would slip out it still seems a bit silly to do things this way.- Speaking of flaps, the main flap of the bag is held quite securely in place with lots of Velcro (in addition to a pair of locking clasps.  That's great until I want to open it and then I get lots of that ripping sound when Velcro is pulled apart.  Other bags I have, such as myThink Tank Retrospective 7 Tall Shoulder Baghave the ability to block some or all of the Velcro if I choose.
summary: A few good features overcome by problems and gaps

title: Canada Goose Ladies Hybridge Hoody
description: Part of Canada Goose's HyBridge line, this hoodie features the company's Thermal Mapping technology, which is the strategic distribution and linking of multi-zone down insulation with a functional secondary fabric within one garment. Two hand pockets with YKK reverse-coil zippers are handy for storing belongings, and the internal stretch pocket is perfect for a cell phone or MP3 player. Other details include a grab strap on the back, elbow articulation for greater movement, and 3M reflective tape around the biceps for increased visibility.The Polartec Power Shield O2 softshell is made with 80 percent polyester and 20 percent nylon and has a fabric weight of 310 grams per square meter (GSM). Its tightly woven face blocks 96 percent of the wind and allows the remaining 4 percent to penetrate and circulate within the jacket, maximizing the warmth-to-weight ratio. This perforated membrane piece offers two times greater moisture vapor transmission than other waterproof, breathable shells. In addition, it reduces the risk of heat stress buildup. This fabric is ideal for any type of cold-weather outdoor adventure, as it has an extremely abrasion-resistant face and a durable water resistant finish to help repel any precipitation.The jacket's lightweight shell is made of 100 percent, 20-denier ripstop nylon with a durable water resistant finish and a fabric weight of 36 GSM. The lining is 100 percent, 40-denier, down-proof, plain-weave, recycled polyester with a DWR finish and a weight of 62 GSM. The insulation is 750 fill power Hutterite white duck down.Product CareWhen your down-filled parka requires cleaning, it is important that you take it to a dry cleaner and that you do not machine wash it. Machine washing your parka will void the warranty. If your parka has a removable fur option, remove the fur ruff before dry cleaning. If you have a small stain on your parka, another option is to spot-wash the parka with a bleach-free detergent and water.Manufacturer's WarrantyAll Canada Goose products are fully warranted against defects in materials and workmanship. If a product ever fails due to a manufacturing defect, the company will repair the product without charge or replace it at its option. This warranty does not include repairs due to accidents, improper care, negligence, or normal wear and tear. In such cases, Canada Goose will repair the item for a reasonable charge. This warranty is valid exclusively in the country of purchase through the original retailer.About Canada GooseCanada Goose has been manufacturing innovative, high-quality outerwear in Canada for over 50 years. From South Pole research facilities and the Canadian High Arctic to the streets of New York City, Stockholm, Milan, Toronto, and Tokyo, people wear Canada Goose products because of the company's reputation for quality, functionality, and style. Its collection of down-insulated, technical, and travel-inspired outerwear offers protection in conditions that range from the mind-numbing cold of Antarctica to the gale force winds on the North Sea.All Canada Goose products are field-tested by those who live, work, and play in the environments they emerged from. From the Constable Parka developed with insights from law enforcement agencies to the Expedition Parka worn by almost every scientist at the South Pole and the Chilliwack Parka designed for pilots of the north, it is safe to say that Canada Goose outerwear is truly a product of its environment.

title: Mountain Hardwear Mesa Convertible Pant - Regular Inseam 32"
description: A classic fit, lightweight, durable Canyon Cloth and zip-off legs highlight these full featured hiking pants. The seamless conical waist provides exceptional comfort under a pack. Features: Articulated knees. Roomy, front pockets. Adjustable drawcord cuff. Seamless waist panel. Zip-off legs. Micro-chamois lined waist. Two rear, open top pockets. Full length inseam gusset. Integrated belt with adjustable buckle. Side cargo pockets with internal reinforcement panels. Mountain Hardwear
reviewText: Short and SweetI have had these for over a year now and wear them at least once a week. There is a design flaw in the pocket which I hope will be fixed soon. When I sit on anything that places my knees higher than my rear things begin to fall out of the pockets. This includes car seats, couches, and recliners. Other than that, love them.ExpandedI purchased these one year ago along with a similar pair of Columbia Silver Ridge II convertible pants which I will be using for comparison. I find myself wearing the Mesa pants much more because of a few key features which I will point out in a moment. First let me lay down my general impressions. They are very comfortable. They have a waist lining which by the manufacturers description is chamois lined and it is very nice indeed. The fabric has held up just fine to regular one to two time a week wear. I have also taken these on several weeks of travel and backpacking. They are light weight (a little heavier than the Columbia), quick drying, and durable enough not to worry about if they are going to snag on a branch. Finally, I just plain like how they look on me.What I LikeThe Mesa pants feature that I like the most is in the waist band. Not the chamois portion, though nice, more specifically it is the belt. The nylon belt is integrated into the pants much like a drawstring, completely enclosed by fabric. On the Silver Ridge the nylon belt goes through loops which sometimes ride up and begin to chafe my sides. Also, the belt being enclosed means that when I wash it, it stays in place unlike the Ridge II pants which comes out, ties itself into knots and then requires rethreading of the belt after each wash (trust me it gets annoying). The best part of the Mesa belt is that it actually works. I find that with the Ridge II pants the belt requires repeated tightening throughout the day. I have finally started tying a knot in the belt so that I would not need to do this. With the Mesa pants I have never needed to do this. Even when I go to the range and have a pistol on my hip for hours at a time I rarely need to adjust the belt on the Mesa pants.What I Don't LikeWhat I hate, and yes there is something that I hate about these pants, is that they are some of the worst pants that I have ever owned for keeping things in the pockets. Now I did buy these on a discount clothing site, perhaps they have updated the design but I nearly stopped wearing these pants because of the pockets. If you have anything that will not grab the netting which the pockets are made of (keys stay put thank goodness) such as lighters, pens, small flashlights, you had better do a quick check of your pockets after getting up from a couch, car, and every time from a recliner. Basically, if your knees go above your rear, your pockets are going to start vomiting out your goodies.RatingI give these pants a three star rating because of the poorly designed pockets. All the other features about the Mesa pants are great, so much so that I still where them more than anything else but the pockets suck. For what it is worth, if the pockets were redesigned I would rate these a high four.Bottom lineI would buy these again because I just plane like them and they work for me. Great belt, bad pockets, fix this MH!

reviewText: When it comes to loading up a web harness or vest for operations, one thing that is not considered by most MOLLE manufacturers is that not everyone is into the commonplace AK / AR platforms. For those of us who carry older bolt-action rifles as part of our gear load, there is no real common way to carry stripper clips or en-bloc clips, unless you want to try fumbling with a general purpose pouch for that effect.Enter the Rothco 2-pocket ammo pouch. These things are perfectly sized for stripper clips and magazines both, or you can use them as a general purpose pouch for anything you need to carry along. Granted, these pouches are not MOLLE equipment, they are designed for use with a pistol belt or similar transport, but if you are wearing a LBV / LBH / Plate Carrier, you should also have a pistol belt for either holsters or drop-leg platforms anyways. I purchased two of these pouches, and each one is on my pistol belt directly behind the drop-leg platforms I use for dump pouch (left) and pistol / medkit (right).For $10, the extra storage is hard to beat. When you need to truck the gear and ammo into the engagement zone, you will need storage, and this adds storage without tying up LBV space. Just remember, if you are going to load a pistol belt up with these, make sure you have a LBV or suspenders set for your belt, or certainly as you start moving you will no longer have the belt.
summary: Old-school ammo pouch, modern day utility!

Or the other issue would be that they were zippered and larger drinks or stuff would cause them to open up or the holders would not be breathable (mesh).  The side holders on this bag are elastic top with a mesh pouch (the perfect combination).  As if that were good enough, Outdoor Products also included a zippered pocket behind the bottle holders.  So this means there are actually 4 side pockets (2 on each side).  The mesh pockets hold my coffee tumbler and my Camelback water bottle very well, even with stuff in the zipper pocket behind them.All in all this is a great bag. description: This bag is perfect for souvenir hunters and anyone who shops impulsively. Heavy duty travel tote with loads of storage space to stow all those purchases. reviewText: First off, I own the little sister matching tote to this bag, which is called the "Reisenthel Mini Maxi Travel Shopper". But the one reviewing right now is the "Reisenthel Mini Maxi Travel BAG", which holds a boat load of stuff.I was torn between the two, so I ended up buying both sizes, and I have to say this one is the BEST bag for carrying along on a plane or even a road trip. I own many reisenthel bags and have a few others that are great for carry-on, but I must admit, after receiving this one, I think its the smartest bag to carry along because it can easily just clip onto your suitcase, carry-on roller bag or even a handbag and used later to carry other stuff when you arrive to your destination, or even use it as a "second" carry-on bag that you can place your handbag or laptop bag inside along with other items making this just one bag and you can still bring aboard a roller bag. It will hold the weight for sure. All the seams and handles are doubled stitched as with all reisenthel bags.What I really like about this bag is the fact it has a full zipper with 2 separate zipper pulls, the handles connect via Velcro, the inside has a key ring loop for easily finding your keys, or anything else you wish to attach to the ring (like a mini flashlight). I especially enjoy the large slip pocket on the outside.  That pocket is something most travelers can appreciate, when they have a boarding pass, phone, water bottle, map, coin purse etc that need a place to put aside briefly until they can use it without unzipping the entire bag looking for the items.If Reisenthel is reading any of these reviews, please keep producing these bags. I think they just may become your number one seller especially for travelers with kids.As I had written in my previous review of the smaller version of this bag, the material is very nice and mostly similar to the material made from a camping tent. It also appears to be very water resistant too.  It comes in a pouch that you can velcro close and use the pouch for other items when the bag is in use, like postcards and maps etc. I so much wished I had this bag when I was in Europe last summer.The dimensions of this bag is approximately 25" wide x 16" tall x 10" deep.  The manufacturer's insert indicates it will hold up to 15kg or 33 pounds. Personally, 33 lbs is pretty heavy. I use a backpack when traveling and as big as it is has never weighed anywhere close to 33 pounds (more like 20lbs max). Regardless, this travel bag will do you good and is definitely worth purchasing to take along. 5 stars for sure!

description: Unlike smooth leather, which can look great distressed and beat up, suede and nubuck leather just looks old and tired. Pedag's Suede, Sheepskin, Nubuck Leather, and Textile Care Kit contains the tools you need to keep your shoes, boots, clothes, and even furniture looking like new. On suede and sheepskin use the brass bristles on the Suede Brush to remove surface dirt. On Nubuck and Textiles use the rubber bristles on the Suede Brush. Nubuck and Textiles are durable but usually not as thick as suede. Next, use the side fan on the brush to remove dirt and debris from tight spots. Use the eraser to very gently remove stains and oily spots(be especially gentle on Nubuck and Textiles). Brush away eraser residue. Shake the container of Suede Care Color Restorer, unscrew the top, and press the sponge applicator against the shoe until the liquid contents start to flow. Evenly cover the surface and allow the liquid to dry for about 10 minutes. The Suede Care Color Restorer renews the color (neutral color will brighten and refresh all colors, but does not add color), while it also helps repel dirt and water. Next use the soft rubber bristles of the Suede Brush to restore the luxurious nap that makes suede and nubuck so lovely. Experiment: brush the suede, sheepskin or nubuck with the grain for a smooth soft color or against the grain of the leather for a brighter color and a different look. Caution: Color Care helps repel water, but it is not a complete waterproofer. Pedag makes waterproofers are ideal for all leathers and textiles, but other manufacturers make suitable waterproofers too. FYI: If your clothing or footwear has high tech, breathable membranes, be sure waterproofers and other care products will not clog the pores that allow air to circulate (products that contain silicone for example). Pedag waterproofers and items in this kit are all compatible with high tech membranes.
reviewText: I bought this kit in "Colorless" when my 3rd grade daughter came home distraught because another kid from school spilled paint all over her suede boots with a Native American style fringe. So the challenge was to remove water soluble white paint that covered about 15% of the surface of her brown suede boots. With a bit of elbow grease I was able to get her boots looking brand new in 20 minutes. The kit was cheaper than buying new boots or paying a professional to do the job.  All in all for my application it worked perfectly.

description: Lightweight, textured mesh fabric breathes for superior airflow. Signature Moisture Transport System wicks sweat away from the body. reviewText: Bought these yesterday at an UA outlet store for $32, and put them to the test today on a very windy cold, 50-54 deg day, 20 mile bike ride on Martha"s Vineyard.  I wore these under a pair of loose fit blue jeans.  I wore a loose fit Under Armor T-shirt top, with along sleeve UA shirt on top of that and a light jacket.After about 8 miles I notice that my legs felt cold, almost a wet feeling despite riding nearly non stop, pumping with my legs did not keep them totally warm.  I also noticed some chafing in the crotch.I had to peal the top jacket off and with it off I felt cold, and with it on I was too warm.  A Gortex shell would have been perfect.  By the way I was very happy with both shirts.My overall impression is these pants don't live up to the hype.  They work, but there are better products out there. I did like the fact that the labels are printed not tagged on the neck--so no chafe there.  There are washing instruction tags on the sleeves of the shirt.  I didn't notice any on these pants.  The seams are well sewn and I don't really notice them except to think that I don't notice them.  You know they have seams, but can't tell where they are exactly.  Unlike some base layer pants I have that are warmer--these sacrifice some warmth for comfort.  My other base layer pants are super tight, twice as warm and less comfortable.The pants work well as a base layer, but I would not recommend them in extremely cold conditions.  I'd use these for less extreme conditions and perhaps as a second layer under my warm base layer.  I was able to slip on a top pant easily.  I definately felt I needed a wind break top layer pant.  I am looking forward to trying them with my offshore sailing gear.  I think they will work OK for wet but not extreme conditions.  Could I wear them three days in a row if stuck in a gale offshore?  Time will tell. I think they will be too cold.I think these might work best as a second or outer layer under a good set of thermal underwear, with perhaps as a middle layer under a light waterproof shell on top for bike riding in cold and wet conditions.UA gives a 10% military discount. I would buy their products again. It is difficult to make a product perfect for all conditions.  These are priced reasonably, do a good job, but you do need to try them to figure out what works best for your type of activity.  Be aware, the slick smooth comfortable feel does tend to feel cold though.
summary: Not Bad, but not as good as I expected

description: Croakies Suiters are lightweight and remarkably soft to the touch -- you may occasionally forget you're wearing them. Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. They've even been used out of this world, having become standard issue on the Space Shuttle in 1990.
reviewText: I used these for a good 2 years on small wire frames.  Was working looking down and these kept me from chronically pushing my glasses back up my nose.  Especially on warm days, when your face a bit more oily.  These were a solution.  Not fashionable, but purposeful.

description: The masterpiece watch winder is ideal for fine watch connoisseurs and collectors. It takes almost 60 days for a skilled craftsman to construct. reviewText: I purchased this winder for a Tissot PRC200 Automatic.  There are 3 settings for this winder.  One of the settings did not work for my Tissot, but the 6min spin every 20 mins works great. Without the winder the watch would die in about 15hrs of non-use. With this winder it has continued to work for 5 days of non-use.  I have an average sized wrist and the clasp does not clasp around the mount.  This is not an issue as it fits in the slot fine and holds in place.While I only have one watch that needs to be wound I have a citizen blue angel sitting in the other winding spot.  The Tissot is not a small watch, but the citizen is.  They almost touch, but as long as the winder is facing out the watches sit fine.  I don't think you could have 2 large watches side by side.The 3 non-wind slots are holding a casio solar watch, a small citizen fraternity watch, and a Large fossil watch.  They all fit just fine.The case itself is stylish looking and fits well on my dresser.  Several people said the case is difficult to keep clean.  I could see how it would be difficult to keep fingerprints off the case and it will probably smudge easily.  The dresser is right next to my bed and it runs 6 mins every 20 mins.  I never hear it running.  Several people have said that over time the winder gets louder, if this happens I will update.Overall this is a quiet winder that works for my watch.  Its too soon to know if its a durable device, but so far its great. With 3 settings you have 3 options to keep a watch wound so it should work with alot of different watches.

reviewText: I love dangles on my Pandora bracelets and I have quite a number of them. I had been buying more expensive carrier beads, but fecided to give these a try.They are OK IF you put a bracelet together and plan to wear that combination of beads and charms for a couple of days or so. They are not good for long term use. I have both kinds of bracelets: a. The kind I put together and like so well that I do not change them...this applies to specific holiday bracelets I have for Christmas, Thanksgiving, Easter, and the Fourth of July. And I have some color combos that look so nice that I do not want to change them. b. The kind that I put together for a special occasion or to go with a specific outfit, and then I take the beads apart and use them for something else. I am a bit of a Pandora charm and bead nut!Over a period of three years I have discovered that carrier beads for dangles come in two varieities: those that will last forever and those that break under the strain of being worn for extended periods of time. These are the later variety. They will, and have broken. It is OK to put a dangle on them if you plan to wear the dangle for a day or two; otherwise, you need a sturdier carrier...one make of sterling that has no joints.I discovered this the hard way. I had two bracelets that I wore for a week and each had three dangles. I had them on these Dragonfly carriers. At the end of the week, I took my bracelets off to clean them and the beads up and to rearrange them. I was sad to find that two of the carriers had broken and I had lost two dangles. Luckily they were not expensive ones. Also I admit that I wore the two bracelets 24 hours a day, slept in them, showered in them, did gardening with them on...the whole thing. I lived in those bracelets for 5 days. A Lesson Learned. These are not sterling; therefore, they are not very hard and repeated banging and jangling by the beads next to them takes a toll on their stength. Also, they are not one solid piece; instead, the loop starts as a separate piece from the Dragonfly which also effects the strenght of the carrier.Sometimes the dangles that I have on my bracelets are fairly expensive...thirty dollars or more. In those instance, I use a carrier bead that will not fail. This is my favorite:Zable Filigree Carriers Sterling Silver Charm. Zable's carrier beads are sterling and made in a mold so that they are all one piece. They are guaranteed.So, If you need a cheapies carrier bead, these are OK, but for your expensive dangles, I suggest Zable.

title: Lowepro LP36407-PAM Pro Messenger 180 AW Backpack (Slate Grey)
description: When your gear feels right, your work goes more smoothly. The Pro Messenger AW - a soft-sided bag that fits pro-sized gear - was designed with this idea in mind.
reviewText: I recently had the chance to review the entire line of the new Pro Messenger series thanks to a brick and mortar shop that sent me the bags I did not receive from Amazon (yes, I had to send them back).  As I stated in my review of the smaller LoweproLowepro LP36406-PAM  Pro Messenger 160 AW Camera Bag (Slate Grey)and the largerLowepro LP36408-PAM  Pro Messenger 200 AW Camera Bag (Slate Grey), I have used LowePro products for the previous 15 years and owned nearly every bag they produced including Fast Packs, Pro Roller (x200 and x300), Slingbag, Stealth Reporter, Event Messenger, the previous Messenger line, etc.... I also owned many Think Tank, Tamrac, and Timbuk2 bags. I admit openly I was addicted to gear bags. Last year, I switched entirely to the Domke brand mainly because, as with many photographers, my shooting style changed. I also chose to go retro with a minimalist approach since I took up street shooting. By comparison, LowePro bags are generally bulkier by design to maximize gear protection whereas Domke bags are designed to be more streamlined, almost in a minimalist fashion. So, when given an opportunity to checkout the LowePro, I was interested.The new LowePro Messenger line could be considered a response to the Think Tank retrospective line such as theThink Tank Retrospective 20-Pinestone Tall Shoulder Bag -, which I owned at one point. That was the thought that came to my mind when I first opened the box. The LowePro Messenger 180 AW (AW stands for All Weather by the way) has the same subdued and non descript approach to gear carrying as the ThinkTank Retrospective line, perhaps more so. Thankfully, LowePro did not place its logo on the bag, making it even stealthier. The bag simply does not look like a camera bag and instead looks like an A-typical messenger or book bag. As with nearly all LowePro gear bags, the build quality is impeccable and to be admired frankly. The fabric (synthetic) feels and acts very close to canvas (called 'Custom Performance Fabric"). It is a bag made to last for a very long time and can take a lot of abuse. It even includes a built in rain cover (bottom of the bag).Like the smaller 160 version and the larger 200 version, the design of this bag clearly seeks to balance the bulkiness of gear protection with ease of carrying. Gone is the bulky and boxy approach to gear protection (LowePro could get very boxy). Inside, you will have room for a DSLR body with grip and three pro lenses or a combination of lenses and flash (3 compartments). As with any bag, you have to compromise. Those wishing to carry all their gear everywhere they travel will need to look elsewhere and go larger; it's that simple. The bag design provides quick access to the gear compartment and retains usability of the shoulder strap and carrying handle when the flap is open. therefore, when street shooting, you could fold the flap over and work directly out of the bag from the shoulder or carry the bag with the handle, a nice feature. The bag also provides very functional pockets including outside flap, inside flap, and another inside the bag. A rain cover is built into the bottom of the bag. The bag also has a luggage sleeve, which I find very useful when traveling through airports. Like Domke bags, the shoulder strap is 3/4 inch wide and disperses the weight of the bag very well (though it is difficult to overload this bag) and also, just like the Domkes,the shoulder strap has a rubberized bottom to keep it from slipping off your shoulder. LowePro also provides a carrying handle that can also be used with the flap open. I can never use a messenger bag that does not include a carrying handle, so that addition really makes a big difference. Finally, the bag closure system was obviously well thought out. Like some Timbuk2 bags that provide silencers for the velcro, LowePro took it one step further. The flap can fold up onto itself, which silences the velcro. However, the flap will then stay shut with magnetic closures, unlike the Timbuk2 design. Also unlike the Timbuk2 design, you stand no chance of losing the silencers (I always lost these).LowePro did a good job with this bag. It's bigger size than the 160 makes it a clearer choice for many, making it less of a compromise. It provides a solution suited for discrete street shooters or urban commuters who wish to carry a camera to and from work. While I am far too attached to my Domke bags to ever drop them (at this point), this type of bag from LowePro gave my Domke a serious run.Considering the sizes available, if I had to choose, I would choose the larger 200 version.  It is not unwieldly and carries just like any messenger bag. I believe many end users will find the bags a little smaller than anticipated once they open the box.  Besides, it is very rare you ever hear a photographer wish their bag was smaller.
summary: Medium Sized Version of a Great Bag

reviewText: Great Captain Rex costume!  A little cheaply made (as expected), but otherwise very cool. Looks good, but no kid would keep this on for very long.  Then again, costume looks great even without helmet.Belt - WAAAAYYYY too big. He wears a 6 Slim in jeans and an XS (5-ish) t-shirt.  Jumpsuit part of the costume fits him perfectly.Velcro closures - the rough side of the Velcro tends to stick to the polyester suit fabric and is hard to un-stick without damaging the fabric.  So, we attach a binder clip to that side of the Velcro (or make sure the Velcro is closed) when we take the suit off so it can't stick to the suit.Not breathable - the suit gets pretty hot & sweaty, so unless you're wearing in cold weather, you probably don't want to wear a shirt under it.Body armor - VERY cool.  It's 3-dimensional, which is hard to see in the picture, made out of a thin foam/soft-flexible plastic.In spite of the above "complaints," we still love this costume.

description: The Timex Men's T5J561 1440 Sport Digital Resin Strap Watch offers a crisp, digital dial with a 24-hour chronograph and a daily alarm. reviewText: I wouldn't buy it again.I thought people said in the reviews that this watch was small.  I found it is rather large gets in the way. I don't have big wrists, but the band needs to angle out a good 30 degrees on both side.  When I set the watch on my arm it is held up about an inch away from my wrist.  This lets junk, dirt, etc get under the watch.  This makes the watch uncomfortable unless it's on the side of my wrist, which is a pain to read.I didn't know before but I hate resin watchbands.  It doesn't breathe at all, making my wrist constantly sweaty and itchy.The final complaint is the window.  It's bubbled so it sticks out above the plastic of the watch. title: Jewelry Silver Dip Cleaner 8 oz.
categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Novelty, Costumes & More', 'Jewelry Accessories', 'Cleaning & Care']
description: Simply Place Jewelry into jar, immerse for 2 minutes. Rinse with hot water and wipe clean with a soft lint free cloth. Can also be applied with a soft cloth to larger items. reviewText: When I first ordered this product it came in a box with no padding and not in a bag, needless to say the container was cracked and leaking. This was the fault of amazon (or at least I thought at the time) who kindly refunded me as they always have exceptional service. I decided to try and reorder it and this time it came nicely padded and not broken but the problem does not end here.After having this cleaner for not very long it is very easy to see why the container broke in shipping, it is absolutely terribly made and I cannot stress that enough. The plastic of both the container and the lid are cheap and very thin. ANY cleaner that is mildly carcinogenic should have a thick and sturdy container with a sturdy lid that has a GELLED seal in order to create the tightest seal. All liquid cleaners I have ever purchased have this except this one (most liquid cleaners are slightly carcinogenic). The foil seal that covers the opening that is removed before using came right off when I just unscrewed the lid for the first time, no seal whatsoever, terrible.After having this cleaner for not too long I traveled somewhere and carried this along with other liquid cleaners with me (I am a jeweler). They were all in separate plastic bags and wrapped individually in bubble wrap to protect them well in my luggage. None of the cleaners broke, except this one. I can't believe the company would produce a chemical liquid in a container this cheaply made. For this reason alone I do not recommend.If you insist on buying this cleaner you absolutely must immediately transfer it to a new leak-proof container. That is if it has not leaked everywhere in your package already.On to the actually cleaner:The cleaner is nothing special. I understand it is desirable to drop jewelry into a liquid and rinse it off to get it clean as it requires no effort, but I can assure you you won't get the results you wish. First off never use this cleaner without gloves on your hands. The directions say to submerse it in the liquid for 2 minutes but I can assure you it takes longer than that. Place silver jewelry one at a time in the liquid for 5 minutes. Remove and rinse thoroughly with hot water for several minutes. Gently pat dry with a paper towel. Place back in the cleaner for another five minutes. Remove and rinse thoroughly again with hot water for several minutes. Depending on how tarnished your jewelry is do this 2-3 times but no more than 3 times. Do NOT leave it in overnight, you should never do that with a liquid cleaner. After you are done wipe down with a basic polishing cloth. I used this for silver chains and only chains because chains trap dirt and oil and trap any other kind of non-liquid cleaner.My advice is to pass on this polish. Check outBlueMagic 400 Metal Polish Cream - 7 oz., I can't recommend it enough. It works on ALL metals, including silver. It leaves them looking shiny and better than new and really puts a seal on it to protect the jewelry. Yes that is a cream which means it requires some elbow grease to scrub the jewelry and may take a while but I can assure you it is worth it. You will be mind blown with the finished product and it will last much longer. Trust me on this. Avoid this product.

reviewText: Bought one of these from Amazon in "bird on a wire" print and one from Amazon via Altrec in the turquoise trimmed floral print for my middle school daughters.  I'd previously purchased them "plain jane" Jansport packs that lasted 5 years each (and still look great!), because they were lightweight, one large and one small compartment and highly durable and comfortable.  While these just came in, my daughters did a test pack of them and they have lots of capacity and are lightweight when empty. I personally would prefer they had no compressions straps which interfere with full zipper openings on at least one compartment, but doesn't seem to bother my kids.  Construction looks durable, I think the Jansport padded shoulder straps were probably more comfortable.  However for the style, capacity, light weight and price I think these are a good purchase.  These are high capacity/large backpacks that I think would be overkill/oversized for a younger elementary student.Update: My middle schoolers packed these full for the school year.  One has held up well, while the zipper on the other's main compartment separated after 4 months and continued to separate (open along the just zipped section) after brief use for the remainder of the school year.  So, I think that packing them full of books/notebooks/etc. will take its toll. I expected these to hold up for 3 years.  Conversely, they carried the same two compartment Jansport for 5 years of elementary school without a problem (much less bulk inside though).  I agree with the reviews that complained about the zippers going all the way to the bottom of the main compartment, a real challenge especially with the zig zag booster cords.  I will consider this as well as other brands for next year's replacement.  They do wash well, and the fabric was sturdy and attractive.

reviewText: If your photo bag requirements tend towards fully fitted SLRs with extra lenses and accessories, this is the bag for you.  It's big and has big carrying capacity with lots of pockets, nooks and crannies for everything you might possibly carry.  Padding is everywhere and adjustable to protect fragile equipment.  It is light weight for its size.The outer fabric is incredibly durable and the two carrying straps provide flexibility for over-the-shoulder or simple side carry and quick pickup.  This is truly a swiss army knife of camera bags.  It's versatile, configurable, well built and well padded.  Did I mention it is large.  Definitely overkill for a standard digital SLR with one extra lens and few accessories.  I would choose Lowepro's next size down for that purpose.Having used this bag on the road for a couple weeks I'm enthusiastic.  I'm coming from a Kato 3N1-22, which has been my workhorse for years.  The Lowepro compares favorably.  Each has it pros and cons.  Really depends on your needs.  The Kato enables a bagpack, sling configuration which the Lowepro does not.  This makes the Kato easier to tote in rugged situations.  I find the Lowepro easier to access when just out and about around town.  The Lowepro has more room for a fully configured digital SLR with attached telephoto lens and other attached devices such as a flash unit.In summary, I suggest you define your needs and check out this bag at a store.  If your needs tend towards a bag with large carrying capacity you won't go wrong here.Highly recommended.

description:
This ultimate gym backpack keeps everything separate and accessible. It can stand or hang in most gym lockers. This bag is also a great size for overnight travel.

reviewText: I love this bag!!!  I am petite (5'0 on a big hair day) and was concerned about feeling/looking like I was hauling a suitcase on my back.  It actually fits quite comfortably, not too oversized, stands firmly and unassisted in the gym locker, and fully-packed is still remarkably light.  Like any bag, it takes a while to develop regular parking places within the bag for your stuff.  The three shelves are relatively deep and flexible; the bottom shelf can hold both my water shoes, and I can cram in my sz 6 sneakers.  Middle shelf holds flat items only; bathing suit, toiletries, and a very small hairdryer can also fit in this level. The top shelf is a nice zippered enclosure which fits a shower wrap, and an uncomplicated summer weight/sized outfit (one pair of jeans and one t-shirt rolled tightly.  Most clever features are the external zippered pouches; they are shallow, nicely accommodate phone, goggles/cap and gym ID, and allow access without having to put the bag down.  Water bottle holder is a seems a bit undersized for larger Camelbak bottles as is the small cell holder pouch in the iPhone era.  Overall, it is sturdy and comfortable to use!

Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. description: Richly detailed and accented with shamrocks, Belleek's Nadine Trinket Box is shaped, painted and glazed by hand in Ireland.  Resting on a delicately scalloped pedestal, the box's cylindrical design opens broadly for easy access to jewelry and trinkets within. A great way to bring a bit of the Irish countryside to the bedroom vanity or bathroom shelf, the Nadine's glossy white, outer walls are sectioned with wavy scrollwork on detailed diamond-patterned embossment and that best-known Irish emblem, the emerald green shamrock. Hand-painted on each glossy frame between the scrollwork, the shamrock's white background accentuates the lifelike green clovers-symbols of health, fame, fortune-and, of course, the luck of the Irish! The trinket box's lid features a ribbed, clamshell-like texture and is crowned with a garland of more clover.Glazed all over, this 2-inch-tall piece is handmade and hand-painted on the Emerald Isle, and crafted of fine Parian China-a material developed by Belleek in the 1840s for sculpting classical figurines with crystalline translucence. The Nadine range of giftware includes votives, vases and candlesticks suitable for all occasions. The Nadine collection coordinates with Belleek's Shamrock pattern, a design created by talented basket weaver, Michael Maguire, which features a meld of basketry and pottery.Since its beginning in 1857, Belleek has been cherished by porcelain aficionados worldwide, and has been sought by royalty, heads of state and museums alike. Regarded as one of the finest crafts ever to come out of Ireland, no other porcelain compares to Belleek's ivory-hued luster. And, as with this finely crafted item, no two pieces of Belleek craftwork are ever the same. With unrivaled attention to detail, every lid; every flower; and every handle is lovingly crafted and painted by hand for an original look and feel that is uniquely Belleek. Belleek means perfection. Back in 1857, the pottery's founder, John Caldwell Bloomfield, declared that any piece with even the slightest flaw should be destroyed to ensure that only the most perfect creations become treasured keepsakes. This commitment holds fast more than 140 years later. As anyone in the Belleek Collector's International Society can attest to; every single piece of Belleek China is made using highly evolved materials and techniques handed down from generation to generation, and is a gorgeous addition to any home.--Brian Olson

reviewText: My dad owned a number of the Seiko dive watches over the years, and I have a number of vintage ones myself.  But I'm currently deployed and the one I brought with me now needs repair. I don't use it as a dive watch, so i can't speak to the diving capabilities, but I am always wearing it, without ever taking it off and it's performed very well (water resistance, rugged survivability.)  I'm pretty hard on my jewelry, and this watch stands up to it.  Unlike my vintage Seikos, the crown doesn't screw down, which threw me a bit; i thought i would bump it or break it, but so far so good.  It glows in the dark with a clear visual.  It also is not very heavy, despite its size -- although I may not be a good judge of that because I like big watches and wear heavy gear often.  I like the rubber band for flexibility, and because it doesn't slide around or bang on computer keyboards like previous linked bracelet bands used to.  The only thing I'm not fond of on the watch is the clasp on the rubber band.  The tongue of the clasp tends to stick out a bit, and catches on clothes and gear.  Overall, I'm a fan.

reviewText: I've been approximating this bag for years by using small, rectangular Lowepro bags that I slip into a larger conventional messenger bag. The advantages to that approach are (1) that it completely disguises the fact that I am carrying camera equipment, (2) the camera is much quicker to reach than with a backpack while being (3) much less intrusive than if it were hanging around my neck. And (4) I can put the inner bag into a bicycle pannier or other container if the shoulder bag is impractical for some reason. The 160AW Messenger Bag preserves all these advantages except the last one, plus it's somewhat smaller and it has a built-in rain sleeve.I have many camera bags in different shapes and sizes. If I'm going to be knocking around town, especially if I want to be able to access gear on the fly or if I am carrying non-camera gear as well that I may need to access, the messenger bag is perfectly practical. I've standardized on Lowepro; the quality is so consistently excellent that I no longer consider alternatives. Also, standardizing on Lowepro means that my collection of the velcroed, padded dividers has become large and I can adapt each bag to just about any use you can imagine.The only disadvantage to this bag is that it never folds flat; whether it has bulky gear in it or not, it takes a lot of space.

title: Accoutrements Horse Head Mask
description: We've discovered yet another universal truth - a person wearing a Horse Head Mask looks downright disturbing. But don't take our word for it, wear this latex mask with realistic fur mane to your next social function and watch as people scramble to avoid you. Fits most adult heads. Bagged with illustrated tag.
reviewText: I solved the problem some reviewers complain about (I think it's the same thing they talk about) -- poor visibility through the mouth and nostrils. In my mask, the roof of the mouth flops down onto the lower jaw, almost completely obscuring my view. It's possible this doesn't happen with all masks.I cut a piece of thick cardboard, with rounded edges, and inserted it into the snout. It forces the width of the snout wider, thus keeping the mouth from drooping down. The cardboard is wedged in good enough that it doesn't slide out, and seems like a long-term solution. The cardboard doesn't block my view out through the nostrils, and completely opens up my view through the mouth.Keep in mind, even with a perfect view, you are like a horse with blinders on, looking through an opening that is maybe the size of a fist... you have to be aware of your surroundings to be safe. I wouldn't wear the mask in an unfamiliar environment.The odor some reviewers complain about exists in my mask... enough that my kids won't wear it, but I don't mind it for the short stints it's on. (Seriously, who is going to wear such a thing for an extended period of time? It's a gag mask and looks fantastic displayed in your home. Every rubber mask I've worn has an odor. I don't think this one is particularly strong.)Also, regarding the 'fits most adult heads' claim... I have a big head and it still works. It's snug, but not uncomfortable, and gives me a slight feeling of claustrophobia when pulling it off, but it works.I recommend buying a Styrofoam head to display the mask (available on Amazon). The horse head is a bit long, but the sturdiness of the neck keeps my mask from topping over. You could also mount the Styrofoam head on a wooden base.

title: Whirlpool 207166 Check Switch
description: This is a genuine replacement part.  The model number and name for the following item is:  Whirlpool 207166 Check Switch
reviewText: Be sure to unplug the washing machine before doing the repair. Also, you will likely need a 4A 3AG fuse since when this switch fails the fuse blows. The auto parts stores have the 4A, while the hardware stores only had 3A or 5A.Un-secure the control panel of the washing machine. You'll need a Phillips screwdriver. Look for the screws on the top of the control panel. Fold out the control panel. Look for the fuse, and the switch will be nearby. Replace the fuse. You might need a small slotted screwdriver to pry it out.I used colored markers on the original part to match the color of the wires of the non-white terminals before removing the wires. You should use a small pair of pliers pulling on the metal terminals rather than pulling on the wires. This might take some effort. Remove the holding screw with a small Phillips screwdriver, then rotate the switch and remove.Assembly is the reverse of dis-assembly. If you can't remember which wire goes where, look at the original part as if it were installed. Now you can be glad that you marked it with the color markers.Tape the box of extra fuses in the control panel. That way you'll know where they are if you need them again, as the mechanical timer ($100) may have been damaged as well.
summary: It fit my washing machine just fine, just pricy
