title: Copper Color Heart-Shaped with Roses Earring Holder / Earring Tree / Earring Oraganizer / Earring Stand / Earring Display
categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Novelty, Costumes & More', 'Jewelry Accessories', 'Jewelry Boxes & Organizers', 'Jewelry Boxes']
description: With its lovely heart shape, this jewelry display provides an attractive way to conveniently showcase an entire collection of earrings--no more searching through cluttered drawers for a matching pair. The unit's broad, sturdy base prevents tipping, while its side wine gently dangles strings of pearls, tennis bracelets, watches, delicate chains, and more. Perfect for use on a bureau, vanity table, or dresser, the unit also offers a unique way to display jeweled ornaments at a boutique, craft fair, or home jewelry show. The harp-shaped holder accommodates up to 70 pairs of wired earrings (each pair fits together into a single hole) or 35 pairs of stud earrings, and measures 11''W x 13 1/2''H.
reviewText: I was originally looking for a Christmas present for my 8-year-old niece who had recently had her ears pierced. After having made the rounds at the local brick & mortar retailers, I had a good idea of what was available as far as design, quality, & price. When I perused Amazon's earring holder offerings, this one popped up & it ended up solving two problems with one click. I bought her some earrings for Christmas, but saved this holder for a St. Valentine's Day surprise.I read the Amazon reviews (all of which dispensed good information) & decided to give it a whirl; when it arrived, I was glad I did. I received it on time & found it nicely bubble wrapped in two layers (one around the individual components & one around the entire set). So that the holder can be shipped flat, the bottom disc (which is hollow on its underside) is sent detached & in a separate bubble wrapper which is then carefully taped atop the bubble wrapping for the heart itself. The disc attaches to the base or apex of the heart (which ends in a bolt) by a nut which can be found screwed to the bolt for shipping. The bolt/nut assembly was true & the completed holder stood straight & stable without leaning or wobbling.Once assembled, the holder is as it appears on the site but is even prettier. The copper color has a muted antiqued or brushed appearance. The floral embellishments are old-fashioned, very attractive, & in keeping with the heart/Valentine motif. The holder is of optimal height & width & would likely be a very nice addition to any bureau or vanity. It showcases the earrings without being overbearing itself.The holes are vertically centered on the bars & uniformly spaced in such a manner that they can accommodate thin or wide-based earrings (i.e. hook/wire/French-back or stem-back). The bars themselves are straight, flat, & moderately thin yet sturdy & so could probably hold some clip-backed earrings as well. The stem & leaf embellishments could probably be used to hang a few bracelets or necklaces. If you don't have a lot of earrings to hang, you might also be able to mount a few select pins from the holes.The left outer leaf arrived very slightly curled but not actually bent or creased; neither the metal nor the finish was cracked. One or two of the reviews had made note of this kind of presentation so it wasn't a complete surprise. However, when I first saw it, I overlooked it because I thought it was intentional shaping. I left it as-is because it did add some dimentional uniqueness to the overall feel.When compared to what was available in the stores, this holder was a clear winner in the areas of unique design, size, stability, & very clearly price...&, it's just pretty.As an aside (& I could be wrong) but after reading the reviews & evaluating the holder upon receipt, it would seem like the manufacturer has taken steps to rectify some of the issues consumers found to be problematic in the past. In any case, I can't wait for my niece to unwrap it. I would buy it again & recommend it without reservation

title: FiveTen Men's Freerider (2012) Casual Bike Shoe
description: To clip or not to clip? Instead, ride free! Designed for downhill mountain bike racers and flat pedal riders, the Freerider from FiveTen offers a host of performance technologies that bring you closer to becoming one with your bike. Its lightweight leather and mesh upper features reinforced stitching, a protective toe box, and full lace-up construction for a precise, durable fit. A Stealth S1 outsole provides a secure grip to keep your feet in place.
reviewText: Looking to try platform pedals (I normally used clipless), I picked the Freerider Scribble model because they were under $100/pair, and appearance-wise they matched my other casual shoes (a pair of DC skate shoes- I used to skate a long time ago!) so if I decided to pull the plug on the whole platform pedal experiment, I could still use the FiveTen's for daily casual. Walking around in the FiveTens when I'm out and about will look normal, compared to if I were to try to go casual with my mountain biking, SPD-equipped shoes.When they arrived at my door, I tried them on for fitment. The FiveTen shoe sizing is about the same as with my Shimano shoes, but if I had to be critical the FiveTen's seem to be a tad tighter on the sides; this is most likely due to the fact that my Shimano SH-MT32L Mountain Bike Shoes have thinner sidewalls, where the FiveTen's have padded sides. It didn't make it uncomfortable though, just a little more snug. The toe area is just as roomy. Since the FiveTen's are a more "casual" shoe with a thick, padded tongue, you don't lace these up as tight as other shoes, but they will stay on just as well.Trying them on the soles are not as stiff as the MT-32L's, but not as flexible as my regular DC skate shoes. The centers feel stiff - good when it's time to pedal, since if it's too soft it would absorb some pedaling power when it's time to hammer down. As for the sole compound, the color combo I chose came with the stickier S1 compound (depending on the shoe color, some come with S1 and some come with a less-sticky "PH" compound) and it was immediately evident walking around in my garage - I could literally hear the soles stick to the bare concrete!Sitting on my bike for a quick test "feel", the first thought through my mind was, "wow - these are sticky!" Once I had my weight on the pedals, the S1 compound stuck like flypaper. I couldn't even slide the shoe around on the pedal, nor could I twist the shoe to change my foot angle. I had to actually lift my foot of the pedal to reposition - and when taking a look at how the shoe touched the pedals, I learned why. The pattern of the sole combined with the sticky rubber compound let the pedal pins lock into the sole; either a pin would sit in one of the many recesses in the sole, or it would sink into the raised portions of the sole. For reference, I was using a pair ofBlackspire Sub4 pedal, 9/16" - blackpedals.With the traction there, the first thing I did notice was that my pedaling was cut in half; because I could no longer use the upstroke when climbing (like you can with clipless pedals), I had to rely on just the downstroke. The second thing that I noticed was that in the beginning I was always stepping on the pedals in different fore/aft position; I got spoiled by the clipless pedal and how it automatically positioned my foot in the right place. However, the next ride afterward I didn't notice those first two complaints anymore. I simply adapted to pedaling with downstroke only, and positioning my foot centered on the pedal quickly became second nature within one ride.I have now converted to platform pedals exclusively because of these shoes. It might be difficult to grasp for long-time clipless users (I was one) but if I had to pick the best "plus" for using the FiveTen's with platform pedals: Freedom. My FiveTen shoe may feel "locked on" with its awesome traction, but the split second I have to move my foot, I don't have to subconsciously remember to unclip first - I just move my foot, and it will move. This actually saved me from a crash recently; I was heading downhill on some rough terrain at speed, and when I got to the bottom the surface turned into loose round rocks - a fast change from the packed dirt at the top and middle of the hill. My front tire got loose at speed, but I lifted my left foot and stuck it out to regain my balance, saving myself from a crash. To be honest, I'm not sure if I could have unclipped in time to do the same, as it was a matter of split seconds between surviving (which I did) and crashing (which, thankfully, I didn't).Everyone who's said that the FiveTen shoes stick like glue are not making it up, these have amazing traction and you would have to feel it to believe it!

reviewText: This is a report rather than a product review.(Sara Lee) Kiwi Camp Dry Mink Oil, sold by amazon.com, comes in a 6-ounce yellow plastic tub.  Here is the description (from kiwicare.com):  "Camp Dry Mink Oil contains a multi-refined oil of mink that penetrates deeply into leather, restoring natural oils while conditioning and waterproofing."If the Camp Dry Mink Oil has anything other than mink oil in it, they aren't telling.  Note the application directions:  "...apply with a soft cloth, working well into leather, particularly around the seams and stitching. Wipe off excess and allow the article to stand overnight before wearing."OK, now lets compare to Kiwi Outdoor Mink Oil, also sold by amazon.com (from kiwicare.com):  "contains a rich blend of mink oil, silicone, and lanolin which conditions and waterproofs smooth leather."Got that?  It's a blend of mink oil, silicone, and lanolin.Directions (from kiwicare.com):  "Work a thin coat of KIWI Mink Oil into leather and seams with a cloth of polish applicator. Wipe off excess immediately, and allow to dry for several hours."Notice the differences?Summary:Outdoor Mink Oil Polish is a blend of 3 major protection ingredients, and you can wear the boots after allowing a few hours to dry.Camp Dry Mink Oil is (ostensibly) only mink oil, and you should let the boots stand overnight before wearing them.But wait, there's more!  This product, Kiwi Boot Protector, an aerosol spray product (sold by Amazon) which is described as straight silicone.  The application directions are much different than either of the two "Mink Oil" products:  "Spray entire surface from 7-10" away with a light, even coat. For maximum protection apply a second coat after 4 hours. Use in a well ventilated area away from heat and flame. Do not use while smoking. Allow article to dry for 24-48 hours."The silicone Boot Protector spray recommends two applications, and up to 48 hours to dry before wearing the boots.Three different products, three different application directions, and all 3 have a similar mission:  protect and waterproof smooth leather.

title: Targus Terra Backpack Designed for 16-Inch Laptops - TSB226US (Black/Red Accents)
description: Terra Backpack with Rain CoverTerra Backpack with Rain CoverTSB226US
reviewText: I really like how comfortable this bag fits on my and fits my gear. I've been using this as my laptop/general gear bag for my photography work lately and it works pretty good. I've even been using it to go to the classes I'm taking for my second degree. It really does a nice job and the padded backing on it makes it really comfortable when carrying my extremely thick books for the classes I'm taking.16.5" screened dell laptop that fits, ever so barely into the laptop pocket but it still fits, it's not too snug but it certainly doesn't slop around. The only thing I would like to see is that the velcro strap for the laptop could be adjustable.Lets start with a PRO/CON list.PROs:~========~Comfort back padding, no more book or laptop edges jabbing you in the backlaptop compartment does fit my slightly larger 16.5 laptopshoulder strap d-rings, plastic but still strong enough for me to attach my USB drive and keys to.RAIN FLY: I really like that it has a rain fly tucked in a compartment accessible from the outside of the bag.strong/padded carry handle: built into the shoulder strapsShoulder straps have re-enforced stitching throughout and also are attached at angles to reduce the stress on the straps, you don't find that too often.Strong stitching: most bags you find at general stores have decent stitching but when you pull on them you can just tell that they wont last as long. The stitching on this bag looks like it will hold to some abuse, many of the stress areas have been re-enforced with extra cross stitching...Main compartment restrictive opening straps: You can undo these as needed but you don't always want your bag to be able to just flop all the way open. I like these and they are adjustable for how much stuff you have in the bag.Bulky zippers, this is often a failing in many bags, but these big zippers look like they will hold up for some time.MP3/Phone pocket in the top of the main compartment with headset hole at the top of the bag (no strap to hold stuff in there though)Breather holes in many areas: helps to get the air out of the bag and also helps to keep the bags inside dry and not allow it to get stinky.Outer zippered compartment has a rubber seal that fits together to help keep water out if it rains.Padded bottom: not many bags have a well padded bottom, this one does.Outer compartment has a rubber cover that the zipper handle fits underneath when closed. Should help it to keep from scratching walls but the one on the bottom of the bag should have this as well...Secondary compartment has many organizational pockets inside: 4 pen pockets, 3 business/credit card sized pockets and 2 mesh pockets below for other smaller items, behind those is a large pocket that stretched the whole panel that has the pen, card, and other pockets. The secondary section that contains this is a decently sized storage area itself and can expand into the main compartment if you wish to organize items that way or if you wish to have more in the main you can do that also. At the top of the secondary compartment there is a strap with a quick hook on it for attaching your keys or a memory wallet too but I think it's a bit flimsy for keys and would say to only put a memory wallet to it at most...CONs:~========~no strap on phone/mp3 pocket on the inside of the bag, this seems kind of odd. I did a quick add in strap with some velcro I had laying around, I made sure to sow it in so I don't have adhesive issues later on.no draw string cord on the side "water bottle" pockets, I find that a little annoying, IDK how long these elastic bands will actually hold up...All in all, this is a pretty nice bag and so far it's been pretty good to me. I switch between this one and another one just because I can but I do rather like this Targus bag over a lot of the others out there...
summary: Targus Terra is a winner of a bag. Fits my 16.5" laptop.

title: Professional Ultrasonic Jewelry and Eyeglass Cleaner Cleaning Machine (White)
categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Novelty, Costumes & More', 'Jewelry Accessories', 'Cleaning & Care']
description:
Clean your fine jewelry, eyeglasses, dentures, electric shaver heads and many more household items with this Ultrasonic Cleaner. The stainless steel cleaning chamber has a 16-ounce capacity and uses ordinary tap water. Simply fill the tank with water and and get professional cleaning results. The quiet, solid state circuitry creates 42,000 ultrasonic energy waves per second, bringing your items to a clean, bright shine without using harsh chemicals or scrubbing. The extreme vibrations created by the device cause even the most stuck on dirt and grime to detach. Millions of microscopic cleansing bubbles clean in ways no hand or brush could match!

Applications: cleans jewelry, necklaces, rings, earrings, bracelets, eyeglasses/sunglasses, keys, gold, diamonds, silverware, precious coins, metal badges, metal watchbands, waterproof watches, shaver heads, razor blades, dentures, combs, toothbrushes, valves, nozzles, machine parts, printer heads, and other valuables!

Professional Uses: jewelers, opticians, collectors, dental labs, dentists, artists.
reviewText: Had this for about a year and at first it seemed to clean glasses and jewelry relatively well. Initially my main complaint was that it only ran for 2 minutes with no time adjustment and many items seem to clean best at around 10 minutes, which meant turning it on many times after it stopped. Shortly after I started using it started buzzing louder and continued to get louder over time, not annoyingly loud, just was no longer quiet as when new. Then the off button stopped working, not a big deal since it only runs for 2 minutes anyway. Then it basically died as it started to run for only about 5 seconds and shut off.  Took it apart out of curiosity and there is a circuit board with a bunch of components and even a fuse, always amazed that something like this can be manufactured and sold profitably at retail for only about $20, but then I'm glad it didn't cost more as it was short lived. I liked how it cleaned when it did work so I may look around for a little better unit with an adjustable time setting.
